articles.title: Joe Burrow is positioned very well to win his first NFL MVP award
articles.summary: Joe Burrow is off to a fantastic start for the Bengals this season.
articles.body:
It has always seemed that at some point, Joe Burrow will win an NFL MVP award.

He has been in the conversation before. In 2024 he might have won had the Cincinnati Bengals simply made the playoffs, but they were not good enough around him.

Burrow is fairly quietly having a season that might be his best in the NFL, and that's saying something. He has 1,653 yards, 15 touchdowns and three interceptions for a team that is now favored to win the AFC North. On the road, in a huge divisional game against the Baltimore Ravens last week, Burrow threw for 249 yards and four touchdowns in the second half as the Bengals came back to win 35-13. That bumped up Burrow's MVP odds in the betting market. BetMGM has him second behind Josh Allen, who has +140 odds (bet $100 to win $140). Burrow is second at +450. That gap should shrink in upcoming weeks.

With the Bengals' soft upcoming schedule, it is very easy to envision Burrow leading the race by the end of November. And him not having an MVP award will probably work in his favor.

Burrow has a chance to put up some ridiculous numbers in November. Here is Cincinnati's upcoming schedule with the opposing defense's rank in DVOA : vs. Titans (32nd), at Falcons (11th), vs. Steelers (7th), at Commanders (23rd), vs. Saints (30th).

That's three great matchups and the Falcons and Steelers aren't as scary as their rankings would indicate. Burrow already threw for 282 yards and three touchdowns at Pittsburgh in Week 3. He could pile up some numbers because he's already one of the hottest quarterbacks in the NFL.

Burrow leads the NFL with a completion percentage of 71.7%. His passer rating of 110.4 would be a career best, and is second to only Jared Goff among quarterbacks with 100 attempts. The Bengals are doing a good job protecting him; his sack percentage of 4.4% is by far the best of his career. That number has never been under 6% during Burrow's NFL career. That can keep Burrow healthy, and when he plays behind a competent offensive line he's going to have some huge games.

Of course, Burrow isn't the only quarterback in the mix.

Jared Goff has a similar argument to Burrow. He has thrown 14 touchdowns with no interceptions. The Lions would likely need to win the NFC North — Matthew Stafford was the first MVP winner from a wild-card team since 2008 — but he's putting up numbers to have his name in the conversation. Burrow has a similar issue, and the AFC North is deep and tough like the NFC North.

Allen is the favorite, and for good reason. He's a great player and has had some remarkable games already. What's working against Allen was a big reason he won the 2024 MVP: Voters like to spread the award around. They bypassed Lamar Jackson for his third MVP in 2024, even though he was voted All-Pro quarterback, to get Allen his first award. Burrow is the best quarterback in the NFL without an MVP and that usually matters even if it's not spoken out loud.

It all lines up for Burrow. He is off to a great start. He has a line that can keep him healthy and throwing from clean pockets. Cincinnati is favored to win its division. He will put up some great numbers in November. And he has the name cache that will make him easy to vote for if it's close with Allen, Jared Goff, Brock Purdy or anyone else.

Burrow won a Heisman Trophy at LSU years ago. He's got a great path to add an NFL MVP award to his case this season.

articles.title: Tom Brady's heartwarming move for children with cancer at charity event caught Buccaneers rookie off guard.
articles.summary: Tom Brady has shared countless memorable moments with NFL players, but one small gesture from his Tampa Bay Buccaneers days continues to stand out.
articles.body: Tom Brady has shared countless memorable moments with NFL players, but one small gesture from his Tampa Bay Buccaneers days continues to stand out. A resurfaced video from 2022 shows the seven-time Super Bowl champion surprising rookie Logan Hall with an unexpected autograph. There was no request, no planned presentation and no grand announcement. Brady simply noticed something special about Hall's shoes and decided to leave his mark. The moment became even more meaningful because the footwear carried artwork connected to a charity supporting families affected by childhood cancer.Tom Brady surprises Logan Hall with an unexpected autographThe incident took place at a charity event connected to Tommy's Place, an organisation that supports families dealing with childhood cancer. Hall, who was beginning his NFL career with Tampa Bay after being selected 33rd overall in the 2022 NFL Draft, attended the event wearing specially designed shoes.The footwear featured artwork linked to children supported by the charity. While Brady was at the event, he noticed Hall's shoes and decided to sign them without waiting for the rookie to ask.For Hall, the unexpected attention from one of football's greatest players was clearly a special moment. The young defensive lineman appeared caught off guard but managed to express his appreciation.He told Brady: “It’s an honour man.”It was a brief exchange, but the surprise made it memorable. Brady had already won seven Super Bowl titles by then, making his signature particularly valuable to fans and collectors. However, this interaction stood out for a different reason. It showed a personal side of the quarterback during an event focused on helping families facing difficult circumstances.Tom Brady and Logan Hall continue their NFL journeysThe two players have since moved into different stages of their football careers. Brady retired from professional football and took on several new roles. He became Fox's lead NFL analyst, acquired a minority ownership stake in the Las Vegas Raiders and continued expanding his business interests.His name also remains highly valuable in the sports memorabilia market. Signed jerseys, helmets and other collectibles connected to the former quarterback attract considerable attention from fans.Hall, meanwhile, continues to represent the Buccaneers. The defensive lineman entered the league with high expectations after Tampa Bay selected him early in the second round of the 2022 draft. His development remains important as he looks to establish himself as a consistent contributor to the team's defensive front.Although the autograph incident lasted only a few seconds, it captured a side of Brady that statistics and championship records cannot explain. For a young player finding his feet in the NFL, receiving an unexpected gesture from a legendary teammate was a moment worth remembering.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Travis Kelce backed $200 million Six Flags shuts down major Cedar Point rides for the rest of 2026
articles.summary: Cedar Point is preparing to close its gates on another season, but the final weeks of 2026 are bringing disappointment for visitors hoping to enjoy one
articles.body: Cedar Point is preparing to close its gates on another season, but the final weeks of 2026 are bringing disappointment for visitors hoping to enjoy one last ride. Several popular attractions have already been marked unavailable, leaving guests with fewer options during the park's Halloween celebrations. The development also puts the spotlight on Six Flags, which has a high-profile connection to NFL star Travis Kelce. As an ambassador and investor in the entertainment company, Kelce has an added connection to the theme park business as Cedar Point approaches its seasonal shutdown.Cedar Point ride closures leave visitors with fewer choicesThe biggest concern for thrill-seekers is the growing list of attractions that will not operate again this year. Gemini and Magnum XL-200 are among the major roller coasters listed as closed for the season. Other unavailable attractions include WindSeeker, Thunder Canyon, Sky Ride, Ocean Motion, Space Age and Planet Snoopy.The timing is particularly important for visitors hoping to experience HalloWeekends before it ends on November 1. Friday, October 30, also brings additional scheduled closures, including Blue Streak, Cedar Creek Mine Ride, Power Tower and Rougarou. Power Tower is also listed as closed on Sunday.Several attractions will have delayed openings at noon between Friday and Sunday. These include Camp Snoopy, Skyhawk, SlingShot, Wave Swinger and others. However, conflicting entries have created confusion, with Gemini and some other rides appearing on both closure and delayed-opening lists. Guests should check the official Cedar Point operating schedule before travelling. Scheduled Ride Closures.Travis Kelce's Six Flags investment adds another layerCedar Point's seasonal shutdown comes at an interesting time for Six Flags, particularly as the company strengthens its relationship with Travis Kelce.The Kansas City Chiefs tight end became a Six Flags investor in October 2025 alongside Jana Partners and other executives. The investment group collectively acquired an economic interest of approximately 9% in the amusement park company.Kelce later became its official brand ambassador in March 2026. His role includes supporting marketing campaigns, creating digital content and helping introduce the company's attractions to new audiences.His connection to the parks is also personal. Kelce has spoken about visiting Six Flags attractions during his childhood, making the partnership more than a celebrity endorsement. PR Newswire +1Meanwhile, Cedar Point has another unusual story making the rounds among its fans. On October 25, an off-duty law enforcement officer reportedly spotted someone covered in blood at a Love's Travel Stop in Milan, Ohio. Police soon discovered that the person was actually a Cedar Point haunted house employee wearing costume makeup.The officer quickly cancelled the request for assistance, saying, “Oops, my mistake. You have a good evening!”With HalloWeekends approaching its final day, Cedar Point still has Halloween entertainment to offer. However, visitors will need to weigh the remaining attractions against the reduced ride lineup before planning their last 2026 visit.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "Children with life-threatening allergies": Brittany Mahomes launches $100,000 food allergy campaign after son's health scare
articles.summary: In 2023, Brittany Mahomes found a way to turn one of the scariest moments of her family's life into an effort to protect other children.
articles.body: In 2023, Brittany Mahomes found a way to turn one of the scariest moments of her family's life into an effort to protect other children. After her youngest son, Bronze, suffered a frightening allergic reaction to peanuts, the Kansas City Current co-owner decided to support families facing similar challenges. Her personal experience became the driving force behind a fundraising partnership with plant-based nutrition brand OWYN, aimed at supporting food allergy research and helping families deal with potentially life-threatening reactions.Brittany Mahomes' son's peanut allergy scare inspired the donationThe incident happened in August 2023, when Bronze was just eight months old. What began as an ordinary day quickly turned into a medical emergency after the infant experienced an allergic reaction to peanuts. Brittany later shared details of the family's rushed trip to the emergency room on Instagram, describing the experience as “scary and frantic.”For the Mahomes family, the incident was a reminder of how quickly a child's health can become a serious concern. Brittany also called the experience “terrifying,” highlighting the fear parents can face when their children encounter unexpected food allergies.Rather than keeping the experience private, she used it to support an organisation working to make life safer for affected families.On Thursday, December 7, 2023, Brittany and OWYN announced a donation-matching campaign benefiting Food Allergy Research & Education (FARE). The organisation is recognised as the largest private funder of food allergy research in the United States.“I am proud to partner with OWYN on this match donation to FARE. This is a cause that is near and dear to my heart given the support that the nonprofit provides to families like ours who have children with life-threatening food allergies,” Mahomes said.OWYN and Brittany Mahomes launch $100,000 FARE campaignThe fundraising partnership formed part of FARE's biggest annual fundraising initiative. Brittany and OWYN pledged to match donations up to $100,000, giving supporters an opportunity to double the impact of their contributions.The campaign also highlighted the challenges faced by households dealing with severe food allergies and sensitivities. OWYN said it wanted to bring greater attention to the issue and encourage more people to support research and affected families.“We are committed to standing with roughly one-third of U.S. households dealing with a severe food allergy or sensitivity, and we’re calling on you to join us,” Mark Olivieri, CEO of OWYN, said. “This medical condition is an undeniable challenge within our food system, and we’re continuing our dedication to tackling it head on with our donation to FARE.”OWYN also became the first brand to receive national recognition from FARE.Donations were accepted through FoodAllergy.org/MahomesOWYN until December 31, 2023. For Brittany, the initiative offered a meaningful way to turn a frightening family experience into support for parents navigating similar fears.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: If you had $6M to spend on a home in Kansas, you probably could not do better than what Travis Kelce bought
articles.summary: Travis Kelce paid just under $6 million in 2023 for a gated estate in Leawood, Kansas, and the numbers on the property explain why it looks like a bargain.
articles.body: Travis Kelce paid just under $6 million in 2023 for a gated estate in Leawood, Kansas, and the numbers on the property explain why it looks like a bargain. The Chiefs tight end got six bedrooms, six bathrooms and more than 16,000 square feet of living space on about three acres, according to TMZ and listing details. The house was first priced at $6.9 million before dropping to $5.9 million. Add a pool with a waterfall, a pickleball court and a mini golf course, and few other $6 million listings in the metro area come close.Travis Kelce's $6 million Leawood home is tough to beat in KansasStart with the size. Kelce's house runs between 16,000 and 17,000 square feet depending on the source, which puts it in a class most buyers at this price never see. In many big metros, $6 million gets a renovated townhouse or a modest home with a small yard. In Leawood, it bought a six-bedroom house behind a gate, with room to spare.The local market explains a lot of this. Kelce's earlier house, a custom seven-bedroom in Briarcliff West, cost him $995,000 in 2019. Six times that amount now gets him a gated estate on three acres, still inside the same metro area. That kind of jump in space would cost far more in Los Angeles, New York or the Bay Area.The extras do the rest of the work. Reports describe a pool with a waterfall, a tennis and pickleball court, and a mini golf course, all on roughly three acres. Sports Illustrated reported that the backyard is also where Kelce proposed to Taylor Swift, a piece of history no listing sheet could have promised in 2023. The house is about 15 miles from Arrowhead Stadium, so the drive to work stays reasonable.The price also moved in his favor. The sellers first asked $6.9 million, then cut it to $5.9 million before Kelce bought it for just under $6 million.Why Travis Kelce wanted more privacyKelce did not leave a bad house. He left an easy one to find. TMZ's sources said the old home was too accessible, and other reports said fans had begun turning up outside once his relationship with Swift became public. The old place is now estimated at just over $1 million, and nobody has reported whether he still owns it.The new address handles that with a gate and a larger lot. That matters for a player whose Chiefs contract, a podcast with his brother Jason and a high-profile partner keep him in front of cameras. His four-year, $57 million extension with Kansas City covered the football side. Sports Illustrated also reports a three-year podcast deal worth more than $100 million.So the price tag is big, but it is not reckless. Estimates of his net worth run from $30 million to $50 million, and one report said he paid with his own money and planned to live there alone. A $6 million house sits comfortably inside those numbers.There is a catch for anyone hoping to copy the move. A house this large usually brings heavy upkeep, property taxes and utility bills on top of the purchase price. That stays true even after a discount. For Kelce, that is a rounding error. For most readers, it is the real cost.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: "Couldn't have envisioned this in our wildest dreams": Travis Kelce and Patrick Mahomes share heartwarming moment with young Chiefs fan after her two open-heart surgeries
articles.summary: For Myka Eilers, meeting Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce was about much more than getting close to her favorite Kansas City Chiefs stars.
articles.body: For Myka Eilers, meeting Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce was about much more than getting close to her favorite Kansas City Chiefs stars. The young football fan had spent much of her early life dealing with a serious heart condition. In May 2022, however, she got a day she had always dreamed of when the Chiefs welcomed her to Arrowhead Stadium through the Make-A-Wish Foundation.What followed was a memorable afternoon filled with football, jokes and a few surprises. Mahomes and Kelce took time to play with Myka, who had her own ambitions of reaching the NFL one day. Her mother, Angela Eilers, later struggled to find words for what the experience meant to their family. Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce give Myka Eilers a day she will never forgetMyka's journey had not been easy. She was diagnosed with pulmonary valve stenosis as a newborn, a condition that affects blood flow from the heart to the lungs. She underwent two open-heart surgeries as an infant. Doctors also warned that she might need another procedure in the future.Still, Myka refused to let her condition define her childhood. She played soccer, softball and football, eventually becoming the quarterback of her flag football team. She also had a big ambition: becoming the first woman to play in the NFL.Her love for the Chiefs led her to make a special wish through Make-A-Wish. She initially wanted to go on a Disney cruise, but the pandemic delayed those plans. She then changed her wish and asked to meet Mahomes.The surprise arrived in 2022 when KC Wolf, the Chiefs' mascot, showed up at the Eilers family's home in Yorba Linda, California, with an invitation to Kansas City.On May 25, 2022, Myka and her family arrived at Arrowhead Stadium. During the visit, she found a personalized Chiefs jersey with her name and Mahomes' No. 15 in the quarterback's locker.The biggest surprise came when she stepped onto the field and met Mahomes and Kelce. Mahomes welcomed her with a fist bump before joking about his place on the team."Don't take my spot, though," the quarterback told Myka as she prepared to throw a pass to Kelce. He added, "You can't throw it too good, you know."Myka took her shot anyway. She delivered a pass straight to Kelce, who encouraged her with a playful, "Downtown, Charlie Brown. We're going deep, alright?"The Chiefs tight end then joined her for more football, turning the meeting into something far more personal than a quick photograph with two NFL stars. Myka's mother shares emotional reaction to Chiefs stars' surpriseThe visit also gave Myka a chance to spend time with Mahomes away from the field. She watched game footage with him, including the quarterback's game-winning touchdown pass to Kelce against the Buffalo Bills in the 2021 AFC Divisional Round.She even signed a one-day contract with the Kansas City Chiefs alongside general manager Brett Veach. It was another special touch for a young fan who had dreamed of being part of the team.Angela later recalled the meeting in an interview with TODAY.com, describing Kelce as "a jokester and a fun guy."She also spoke about what the entire experience meant to her daughter and the family. Speaking to Make-A-Wish, Angela said, "Today has been amazing. It's made her feel so special. Our family just feels welcome and seen. We couldn't have envisioned this in our wildest dreams."Myka also remembered the players warmly, telling TODAY.com that Mahomes and Kelce were "really nice and funny; just good people."For a young girl who had faced two open-heart surgeries before she could even understand the game she loved, the day offered something she could carry with her long after leaving Arrowhead Stadium. Mahomes and Kelce did more than meet a young Chiefs supporter. They gave her the chance to step onto the field, throw passes with her heroes and feel like part of the team.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: How Patrick Mahomes’ $1.625 million Boys & Girls Clubs commitment compares with Travis Kelce’s nearly $2 million charity impact
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce both wear Chiefs red, both earn Walter Payton nominations, and both have built a name for giving.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce both wear Chiefs red, both earn Walter Payton nominations, and both have built a name for giving. Their headline figures look close. Mahomes and his wife Brittany announced $1.625 million for Boys & Girls Clubs of America in October 2023. The Chiefs say Kelce has given nearly $2 million to Operation Breakthrough over the years. But the numbers measure different things, over different spans, for different causes. Here is what each one covers, and what it leaves out.How does Patrick Mahomes' $1.625 million commitment compare with Travis Kelce's nearly $2 million?Travis Kelce's total is bigger, but only by a few hundred thousand dollars, and the two figures are not built the same way.Patrick Mahomes' $1.625 million is one announced package. The 15 and the Mahomies Foundation revealed it as a contribution paired with a multi-year commitment. Kelce's number comes from Chiefs.com, which says he has put nearly $2 million into Operation Breakthrough through personal donations and directed funds. One is a pledge made on a single day. The other is a tally built across more than a decade.The destinations differ too. Mahomes' money goes to a national organization, with a focus on places that shaped him and Brittany: Greater Kansas City, Lubbock, Tyler and Whitehouse in Texas. Kelce has stuck with one Kansas City program for years. Focus tends to produce results you can point to. A wider spread buys reach.It also helps to know who is counting. Both figures came from parties with a stake in the story, a foundation in one case and a team in the other. Neither is an audited total. Treat them as fair markers, not final scorecards.What the Patrick Mahomes pledge actually pays forThe details are more concrete than the headline suggests. To mark the partnership, the Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Kansas City and the Boys & Girls Club of Lubbock will each rename one facility after "15 and the Mahomies." The foundation will help upgrade those buildings. The East Texas site, run through The Mentoring Alliance, will fund scholarships for up to 300 young people to attend every year.There is a running meter as well. The foundation said it would give $1,500 for every touchdown Mahomes throws or scores in the 2023 regular season. A 30-touchdown year would add $45,000. That is small next to the main gift, but it ties the cause to game day.The personal link is real. Brittany attended a Club as a kid, and Patrick framed the gift around that: "Kids who attend a Boys & Girls Club, like Brittany once did, are provided with the necessary tools and resources to help this generation not only thrive but lead with compassion and purpose." In the launch video he added, "We hope you'll join us in supporting the awesome work of the Boys & Girls Clubs, because we all know great futures start here."Scale matters here. BGCA says it has more than 5,200 Clubs serving 3.3 million young people. A gift of this size will not change that math. Renamed buildings and 300 scholarships, though, are things a family in Lubbock or Tyler can actually see.Where Travis Kelce's money went and why the Ignition Lab stands outKelce's giving has one main address. Soon after arriving in Kansas City, he leaned into Operation Breakthrough, a nonprofit that provides education and support to children in poverty. His biggest swing was the Ignition Lab, which opened in fall 2021 after his backing helped turn an abandoned muffler shop into a working space. Teens aged 14 to 18 spend time each week building real-world skills, including computer repair, cooking and digital media. The first class graduated with internships and credentials in hand.The dollars stack up. A February 2024 item from a trade group said his foundation had given over $1 million to Operation Breakthrough. In 2020, it gave $26,000 to help the agency keep its doors open. In January 2026, Kelce became the first three-time winner of Nationwide's Charity Challenge, which earned $35,000 for the Ignition Lab. His foundation also gave $100,000 to the Reyes family after the 2024 Super Bowl parade shooting.So the contrast is about depth. Mahomes' pledge is spread across several cities. Kelce's money has compounded inside one building and one program, year after year.The scrutiny question hanging over one of these numbersHere the two stories split. In late December 2025, The Arizona Republic reviewed federal filings for Kelce's Eighty-Seven and Running Foundation. It found the charity reported spending about 41 cents of every dollar on charitable activity from 2021 to 2024. It also paid hundreds of thousands of dollars to A&A Management Group, a firm co-founded by Kelce's longtime business managers.Executive director Aaron Eanes said expenses were wrongly labeled on tax forms for nearly a decade. He said management fees dropped in 2024, fell to zero in 2025, and that filings are being corrected. "We are dedicated to ensuring this foundation operates at the highest standards," he said.Kelce also sent his $35,000 Charity Challenge prize to Operation Breakthrough instead of his own nonprofit. CharityWatch CEO Laurie Styron called that the responsible short-term move. That scrutiny is about the foundation's overall spending, which is not the same as the nearly $2 million the Chiefs tie to Operation Breakthrough. The team describes that money as personal donations and directed funds.On the Mahomes side, searches turned up no comparable reporting about the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation. The launch materials also do not lay out a payment schedule. Readers who want certainty should check the foundation's annual tax filings as they appear.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Kylie Kelce had little patience for strangers questioning why her family owns several neighboring properties.
articles.body: Kylie Kelce had little patience for strangers questioning why her family owns several neighboring properties. The wife of former Philadelphia Eagles star Jason Kelce recently explained that the decision has less to do with owning more real estate and more to do with protecting her family. During an October 29 episode of her Not Gonna Lie podcast, Kylie recalled confronting an Instagram account that shared an aerial view of their home. What followed was a heated exchange about security, privacy and the limits of public curiosity.Kylie Kelce explains why her family bought neighboring homesThe issue came up while Kylie was speaking with comedian Nikki Glaser about the kind of criticism public figures face online. She recalled seeing a post from the Instagram account Celeb Homes, which had shared an aerial photograph of the property she shares with Jason and their four daughters.The post went beyond showing the family's home. According to Kylie, it also included details about the property and its surroundings. That did not sit well with her, particularly because the post offered strangers a closer look at where her children live."They put a bird's eye view of where we live with our children, and they were trying to give details of our property," she explained.The discussion became more frustrating when people began questioning why the family had purchased another house next door. Rather than ignore the comments, Kylie decided to make her reason clear."They were like, 'why would you need this many houses?' And I'm like, 'for [expletive] security and privacy, you pieces of [expletive],'" Kylie recalled.For the Kelces, the neighboring properties serve a purpose beyond adding to their real estate holdings. Having control over the surrounding space gives the family more privacy and security, especially with four young children growing up in a household that attracts considerable public attention.Jason and Kylie married in 2018 and are parents to Wyatt, Elliotte, Bennett and Finnley. Their family life has become a subject of public interest, but that does not mean Kylie is comfortable with strangers examining the details of their home.Kylie Kelce admits she couldn't resist responding to criticsKylie also revealed that she did not limit her reaction to discussing the incident on her podcast. She went directly to the Instagram post and left a comment explaining why the family wanted the neighboring properties."Why would anyone need three neighboring properties? For safety, privacy, and security. Get the f outta here," she wrote.She had apparently intended to make her response even stronger, but Instagram's content restrictions got in the way."I think I typed 'get [expletive].' And then when I tried to post it, it wouldn't let me," she joked. "Why? I want to tell people to get [expletive]."Her exchange with Glaser offered another glimpse of Kylie's approach to online criticism. She is generally comfortable sharing parts of her life with an audience, but there is a clear difference between public attention and strangers trying to establish details about her children's home.The Kelces' fame may make their property an interesting subject for social media accounts, but Kylie is drawing a line between curiosity and personal security. She was not interested in defending how many houses her family owns. She wanted people to understand why keeping their surroundings private matters.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. "Cardinals RB Jeremiyah Love will play Sunday vs. the Cowboys," ESPN's Adam Schefter wrote on his official X account on Friday.

"Jeremiyah Love a third straight practice and deemed go to go against Cowboys by Arizona Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur," Cardinals reporter Bo Brack wrote on his official X account.

articles.title: Week 8 Waiver Wire Top Targets For This Week's Injured Fantasy Football Stars
articles.summary: The Carolina Panthers and Green Bay Packers kicked off Week 8 on Thursday night in a game that could have meaningful playoff implications. Many fantasy managers will be battling for playoff positioning this week as well.
articles.body:
The Carolina Panthers and Green Bay Packers kicked off Week 8 on Thursday night in a game that could have meaningful playoff implications. Many fantasy managers will be battling for playoff positioning this week as well.

Unfortunately, many of those same managers will be without some of their top stars. The Houston Texans, New Orleans Saints, New York Giants, and San Francisco 49ers will all be on bye this week. As has been the case for most of the NFL season, injuries are also a significant factor.

Here, we'll dive into the Week 8 injury report , provide rankings for the top remaining point-per-reception (PPR) plays, and highlight sleepers who may still be available entering the weekend.

The big fantasy news at quarterback is that Baltimore Ravens star Lamar Jackson (ankle) plans to make his return to face the Buffalo Bills this week.

Geno Smith looms as a viable streamer, and he's worth spot-start consideration this week. The former Las Vegas Raiders starter is coming off a 24.5-point outing and will face his former team in Week 8.

The Raiders have surrendered an average of 20.8 fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks this season.

Smith is rostered in only 24 percent of fantasy leagues. Michael Penix Jr., Baker Mayfield, Malik Willis and Jacoby Brissett are other quarterbacks to consider targeting on the wire.

Jets running back Breece Hall could make his return from injury this week and is officially questionable. So is Tampa Bay Buccaneers back Kenneth Gainwell. Atlanta Falcons No. 2 back Brian Robinson Jr. is out.

The Arizona Cardinals could have standout rookie Jeremiyah Love back this week as well.

However, Love may not be back to 100 percent yet. Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley is definitely not, though he could still give it a go against the Washington Commanders on Sunday night.

Tyjae Spears and RJ Harvey are out, while TreVeyon Henderson is questionable.

With Love looking less than 100 percent, Cardinals backup Zonovan Knight is a waiver option worth considering. He appears to have overtaken Tyler Allgeier during Love's absence, and he has topped nine fantasy points in two straight games.

Knight will have a favorable matchup this week against the Dallas Cowboys, who have surrendered an average of 22.6 fantasy points to opposing backfields.

Cleveland Browns running back Dylan Sampson is another strong option in PPR leagues. He made his 2026 debut in Week 7 and finished with 10.7 fantasy points. He'll face a tough Pittsburgh Steelers defense, but he has a lot of upside as a pass-catcher, especially if Cleveland lands in another early hole.

Knight and Sampson are rostered in 13 percent and 15 percent of leagues, respectively. Mike Washington Jr., Samaje Perine, and Chris Rodriguez Jr. are other wire options who may still be available.

Buccaneers wide receiver Emeka Egbuka has cleared the concussion protocol but will not return to face the Falcons on Sunday. He has already been ruled out, along with Bills wide recever Tyrell Shavers. Bills receiver D.J. Moore is officially questionable.

Rashee Rice appears on track to play for the Kansas City Chiefs. Ja'Marr Chase appears set to go for the Cincinnati Bengals. However, DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks will both be out for the Eagles again.

Tre' Harris and Ladd McConkey are expected to suit up for the Los Angeles Chargers.

Carnell Tate will be out for the Tennessee Titans, while Calvin Ridley is questionable. A.J. Brown, George Pickens, Jaylen Waddle, Jakobi Meyers, Olamide Zaccheaus, and Jack Bech are also among the list of receivers who are questionable this week.

It's worth checking to see if Jets rookie receiver Omar Cooper Jr. is available, as he's rostered in 54 percent of leagues. Cooper has topped 20 fantasy points in consecutive weeks and has another reasonable matchup against Las Vegas this week.

Colts receiver Keenan Allen might be a slightly more realistic target, as he's only rostered in 48 percent of leagues. He only had 6.1 fantasy points last week, but he topped 16 points two weeks ago and has another favorable matchup.

The Colts will battle the Jacksonville Jaguars, who have surrendered the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing receivers.

Washington Commanders rookie Antonio Williams hasn't reached double-digit fantasy points since Week 1. However, he's in line for an expanded role following Terry McLaurin's season-ending knee injury.

Williams will face an Eagles defense that has surrendered the second-most fantasy points to opposing receivers. He's only rostered in 15 percent of leagues.

Ja'Kobi Lane, Caleb Douglas, Keon Coleman, and Demario Douglas are other sleepers to consider targeting on the wire this week.

Bills tight end Dalton Kincaid is officially questionable with a chest injury.

If Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson is available in your league, grab him. He's rostered in 63 percent of leagues, and that number is too low, given Minnesota's Week 8 matchup.

Hockenson is coming off a 13.5-point performance and will face a Detroit defense that has surrendered an average of 24.7 fantasy points to opposing tight ends.

Commanders tight end Chigoziem Okonkwo has a less favorable matchup against Philadelphia (8.2 fantasy PPG allowed) but is also more readily available. He's rostered in 25 percent of leagues.

Okonkwo has had back-to-back games with double-digit fantasy points, and he could also see an expanded role with McLaurin done for the rest of the season. Mason Taylor, Tyler Higbee, and Mike Gesicki are other TEs to consider off the wire this week.

*Fantasy scoring and roster information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: Other Women Contacted Police About Previous Incidents with Packers' Josh Jacobs After His Arrest
articles.summary: As police investigated whether to file charges against Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs following a May altercation with his then-girlfriend, multiple other women contacted them to detail their own allegations against him.
articles.body:
As police investigated whether to file charges against Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs following a May altercation with his then-girlfriend, multiple other women contacted them to detail their own allegations against him.

Those accounts were included in evidence regarding Jacobs' battery case that the Hobart/Lawrence Police Department released Friday night in response to a public records request. Green Bay TV station NBC 26 first reported the records release.

Jacobs pleaded no contest Sept. 10 to misdemeanor counts of battery and criminal damage to property. Jacobs was arrested May 26, three days after an incident in which a woman said he threw her to the ground.

Predicting Every Team's Trade Deadline Strategy 🧠

According to the records that were released Friday night, one woman contacted police after Jacobs' arrest to say she had experience a similar incident with him around 2023. She later would say the incident actually occurred on Jan. 5, 2022.

The woman said she had communicated with Jacobs for about six months before spending about 11 hours at his home. The woman said that after she told Jacobs she hadn't come there for sex, he became angry, slapped her across the face and told her not to disrespect him.

She said he took her phone and threw it into a swimming pool when she attempted to leave, and that he grabbed her by the hair, threw her onto a bed, pinned her down, threw her to the floor and said that "I should kill you right now." She said Jacobs also spit on her.

The woman said that she hadn't previously reported the incident to law enforcement because she remained friends with Jacobs afterward and was concerned her allegations wouldn't be believed. The woman said she contacted police this time because she believed it showed a pattern of behavior similar to the allegations in the May case.

Another woman told police she had sex with Jacobs in April 2021. The woman said that his condom broke, so she told Jacobs to get tested for sexually transmitted diseases because they both had been involved with other people.

The woman said Jacobs later removed her from the residence, grabbed her by the arms and bicep area, pushed her against a wall and threw her belongings out. She told police that she sustained bruises to her arms and swelling in her rib area.

Hobart/Lawrence police said they obtained records from that incident indicating officers observed "no visible signs of injury, bruising or damage consistent with a physical altercation."

Another woman said she met Jacobs through social media and that he flew her to a residence in May 2022. She described an altercation in which Jacobs grabbed her by the hair, placed his hands on her head and neck, dragged her, scratched her chest and took her phone after it fell to the floor.

The woman said she got bruises on her arm and scratches to her chest and neck. She said she didn't report the incident to police because she wasn't a U.S. citizen at the time and that Jacobs told her she could be deported.

The records released Friday also offered more details of the May 23 incident that led to Jacobs' arrest. According to the criminal complaint released in August, the woman told them that Jacobs grabbed her and threw her to the ground as she was trying to exit a garage door, causing her to hit her head. Police said Jacobs also took her phone from her while she was on the ground.

The records released Friday noted the woman said that while they were still in the home, Jacobs lunged at her, pinned her on the bed with his body weight on her chest, and that he put his hand on her mouth and nose, so that she felt she couldn't breathe.

She also indicated that she believed she lost consciousness for a brief time when the confrontation moved to the garage.

Jacobs has played two games with the Packers since being removed from the commissioner's exempt list, which had prevented him from playing or practicing with the team. The NFL placed him on that list in August after charges were filed against him, and that caused Jacobs to miss the Packers' first six games of the season.

The NFL is still investigating Jacobs over the incident that led to his May arrest, so the league still could hand out more discipline to the three-time Pro Bowl running back.

articles.title: New Jonathan Taylor Trade Rumors Update Colts' Stance on Dealing RB Ahead of 2026 NFL Deadline
articles.summary: In the wake of trading Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner this week, the Indianapolis Colts are opening the door to potentially moving Jonathan Taylor ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
articles.body:
In the wake of trading Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner this week, the Indianapolis Colts are opening the door to potentially moving Jonathan Taylor ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

Per ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , the Colts are "open" to trading their star running back and are in "active and ongoing" discussions with multiple teams that have reached out.

The Minnesota Vikings, Denver Broncos, Green Bay Packers and New York Giants have been mentioned as potential teams of interest. It's unclear if Josh Jacobs' return would change the Packers' approach.

Cam Skattebo has been up and down in his first season with head coach John Harbaugh, but he's also coming off a career-high 124 rushing yards in the Giants' 27-21 victory over the Houston Texans in Week 7.

Per The Athletic's Jonathan Jones , the Vikings and Giants appear to be favorites for Taylor right now.

As for the cost to acquire Taylor, ESPN's Jordan Raanan has reported the Colts are seeking a second-round draft pick and "possibly more" in exchange for the 27-year-old.

However, Jones noted Minnesota's cap situation would require some maneuvering since the club currently doesn't have enough room available to fit Taylor's remaining cap space.

Addressing his status with the Colts during a media session after Friday's practice, Taylor made it clear he has not requested a trade while acknowledging he doesn't have "full control of his future."

There had been skepticism around the NFL about the Colts possibly trading Taylor after dealing away Nelson and Buckner.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported on Wednesday there has been "heavy interest" in Taylor, but opposing clubs "aren't totally sold" he will be moved.

Despite the overall struggles for the Indianapolis offense this season, Taylor remains a bright spot. He is tied for the NFL lead with eight rushing touchdowns and ranks fifth with 587 rushing yards.

The Colts have lost three straight games and are 2-5 overall this season. They haven't made the playoffs since Taylor's rookie year in 2020 and haven't finished over .500 since going 9-8 in 2023.

articles.title: Former NFL QB Philip Rivers has become a serious option for NC State opening amid college football carousel
articles.summary: Wolfpack donors are rallying NIL resources and gauging Philip Rivers' interest as NC State's coaching search heats up after Dave Doeren's firing.
articles.body: ATLANTA - Former NFL quarterback Philip Rivers has been a topic of conversation around college football over the past week amid the opening at NC State, after head coach Dave Doeren was fired last Saturday. In the days leading up to athletic director Boo Corrigan deciding to make a move with the football program in Raleigh, the talk of Rivers being interested in the potential opening at his alma mater began to pick up within the industry. On Friday night, the former NC State quarterback was walking his son Gunner Rivers onto the field in Fairhope, Alabama, for St. Michael Catholic's senior night, where Philip has served as head coach for the past six seasons. "There's nothing there at this point," Rivers told Ben Thomas on Friday night when asked about NC State opening. "You understand the chatter that is out there. Just gotta take it one day at a time is all I know. I'm excited about the postseason with these guys here. "It's like I told you last year, you never say never. But, there's nothing imminent." COLLEGE FOOTBALL COACHING CAROUSEL COULD EXPLODE AS LINCOLN RILEY AND DEION SANDERS FACE MOUNTING PRESSURE But in Raleigh, NC State administrators and boosters have been putting together a plan in hopes of luring Rivers to the sidelines in college football. As OutKick has previously reported, and confirmed On3's Friday report, Wolfpack donors have been discussing the ways in which they could raise the money needed from an NIL perspective to have NC State more competitive in luring talent to Raleigh, with recent talks also focused on if Philip Rivers were to be hired as the next head coach. These conversations have involved the former NFL quarterback's representation, while also gauging the temperature of those within the Wolfpack donor base if they were to officially offer Rivers the job. At this point, Philip has made it clear he is focused on making sure his team, St. Michael Catholic, was prepared for its regular season finale on Friday night and the upcoming high school playoffs that are set to start next week in Alabama. COLLEGE FOOTBALL’S JERRY JONES? TEXAS TECH BOOSTER CODY CAMPBELL DEMANDS RETURN ON INVESTMENT Rivers will coach St. Michael Catholic next week against Glenwood, with many expecting them to win, which would then lead to another game the following week in the playoff format. From a fan perspective, it's obvious that the Wolfpack would be making a hire that would excite the base, and more importantly help sell tickets and also lead to an influx of donations needed for NIL purposes to compete for an ACC title, and potentially a spot in an expanded college football playoff. NC State needs financial backing to compete, which Rivers could garner But, you also have to be able to raise enough money to compete, as now former head coach Dave Doeren mentioned this past week during a press conference to reflect on his tenure in Raleigh. "The resources need to match the expectations," Doeren mentioned. "I hope for NC State this commitment to football really happens. I pray for the next head coach that he has the opportunity. It's not the way it used to be." Multiple people along the Gulf Coast in Alabama have mentioned to OutKick that they are hopeful that Rivers would take the job if formally offered by NC State, given how highly regarded he is within the community along Mobile Bay. MAHJONG IS THE NEW TAILGATE GAME TAKING OVER COLLEGE FOOTBALL FOR WOMEN — AND EVEN AT HOME WITH HEAD COACHES In speaking with sources close to the situation, NC State is comfortable with the fact that Rivers would be a first-time college football head coach, especially if he puts together the right staff to come with him. Also, his son Gunner is committed to the Wolfpack, and will enroll next year as a freshman quarterback in Raleigh. Could all the stars be aligning for NC State to bring their former quarterback home to lead the football program? Just last week, NC State alum and donor Dr. Andy Albright made it a point to post on social media that he had Rivers with him on his private jet that is decked out in Wolfpack colors. Wolfpack could benefit from a hire like Rivers that would attract players That could possibly be decided within the next week or two, though Rivers is focused on his high school job at the moment. As for this era in college football, it would be a risky, but splashy, hire for NC State, and much different than UAB hiring Trent Dilfer from the high school ranks in 2022. One of the problems for Dilfer was that the former Super Bowl champion could not garner enough support from the Birmingham community and Blazers donor base, mixed with questionable decision making by the UAB athletic department across multiple sports. In Raleigh, Wolfpack athletic director Boo Corrigan brought in former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Bill Cowher earlier this week to help with the coaching search. And while there have obviously been conversations around the prospect of potentially hiring Philip Rivers, NC State has been in communication with a number of agents who represent coaches within the sport to gauge their interest over the past few days. Also, NC State needed to get this search underway as soon as they realized Dave Doeren was not going to be the guy to lead this program into 2027, thanks to ongoing negotiations with current players and having to put a plan together in order to attack the transfer portal. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD It will be an interesting two months across the sport, with Maryland and Baylor also searching for a new head football coach after making their own moves in the past week. The carousel has only just started, with a number of additional jobs potentially opening across the country over the next month.

articles.title: New NFL Trade Rumors on Garrett Wilson, Chances Jets WR is Moved Amid Buzz at 2026 Deadline
articles.summary: Already loaded with a tremendous amount of 2027 draft capital, the New York Jets don't plan to move Garrett Wilson before the trade deadline to add more to their cache.
articles.body:
Already loaded with a tremendous amount of 2027 draft capital, the New York Jets don't plan to move Garrett Wilson before the trade deadline to add more to their cache.

ESPN's Adam Schefter cited a well-placed source who said there is "no way" the Jets trade Wilson before the Nov. 10 deadline.

Schefter added the Jets have "no interest" in dealing their star wide receiver, who is loved by people at the top of the organization and they "would want no part" of trading Wilson.

Insider: 'All Hell' to Break Loose at Deadline

Wilson's name has been speculated about in trades for some time, but it increased during the Jets' Week 7 loss to the Miami Dolphins. He was seen on the CBS telecast at one point in the fourth quarter having what looked like a heated discussion with quarterback Geno Smith and pass game coordinator Seth Ryan.

Wilson downplayed the interaction after the game, telling reporters he was just "disappointed" with how the team was playing.

"We were collaborating. I don't even think I was talking to Geno," Wilson said. "I think we were both heated, but not at each other at all. We were just disappointed with how we were playing up to that point and wanted to be a little more aggressive."

Head coach Aaron Glenn said on Monday the situation was being "overblown" and Wilson was trying more to hype up the offense to get that unit going.

Amid the ongoing trade speculation, Wilson told reporters on Wednesday he has no intention of asking for a trade and wants to remain with the Jets.

There hasn't really been any substantial talk of Wilson being moved at this point. Some of it is because the Jets don't really need draft assets and he can be a huge value to them, especially if they add a young quarterback in the 2027 draft.

New York already owns three first-round picks in the upcoming draft. Based on the current standings , all three selections would be in the top 12.

Wilson is only 26 and has four years remaining on his current contract after this season.

Even with all of the struggles the Jets have had so far in 2026, Wilson is on pace for his fourth 1,000-yard season in five years. He has 444 yards and three touchdowns through seven games.

articles.title: How rich is Jerry Jones? Breaking down the Cowboys owner's net worth, business empire and NFL fortune
articles.summary: Jerry Jones is worth somewhere between $13 billion and $23 billion, depending on who is counting.
articles.body: Jerry Jones is worth somewhere between $13 billion and $23 billion, depending on who is counting. Forbes put him and his family at $20.3 billion on its 2026 world list, and its latest report lists him at $23.2 billion. The Dallas Cowboys, which he bought for $140 million in 1989, are now valued at a record $17 billion. That gap between estimates shows how hard it is to price a man whose biggest asset has never been for sale. Here is what he owns, how he built it and which numbers deserve trust.How rich is Jerry Jones right now?Pick a source and you get a different answer. On the Forbes world list, Jones and his family rank No. 128, up from $16.6 billion in 2025. The live figure has since climbed, and it makes him No. 9 on Forbes' list of the richest U.S. sports team owners. Celebrity Net Worth still carries $13 billion. That number looks dated, because it matches what Forbes said the Cowboys alone were worth last year.Why such a spread? Nobody can read Jones's bank statements. He owns a private team, private land and private energy investments, so every outlet has to estimate. Some update when the team's value jumps. Others lag behind.Treat all of them as informed guesses. The safest reading is that Jones sits above $20 billion on the best-sourced tracker, and that the franchise drives most of it. All figures here are estimates as of late October 2026.From a $140 million purchase to a $17 billion teamJones bought the club from Bum Bright in 1989. The first season ended 1-15. He had just fired Tom Landry, the only head coach the franchise had ever known, and taken over football decisions himself. Dallas was not happy. Then things flipped fast. Jimmy Johnson, his old Arkansas teammate, built a roster that won Super Bowls XXVII and XXVIII, and Barry Switzer added XXX after the 1995 season.The Johnson partnership broke apart in 1994 over credit and control. Years later, asked why Johnson still has no spot in the team's Ring of Honor, Jones said: "Disloyalty … I couldn't handle the disloyalty." It is a revealing line. It shows how personal this business has always been for him.The titles stopped after that January 1996 win. The money did not. Forbes ranked the Cowboys first for the 20th straight year, ahead of the Rams at $13.5 billion, the Giants at $12 billion and the Patriots at $10.6 billion. Dallas generated nearly $1.28 billion in revenue last season, slightly more than Real Madrid, and an estimated $677 million in operating income, $342 million ahead of the next-best NFL team.Pause on that. A team that has not won a Super Bowl in three decades is still the most profitable operation in sports. Winning helps, but ownership at this level sells attention, and Dallas has more of it than anyone. Seattle's $9.6 billion sale to Vinod Khosla shows how fast the whole league is rising, yet the Cowboys still sit far above it.The business machine around the starJones did not just hold the asset and wait. Early in his tenure he pushed for Fox to become a major NFL television partner while older networks wanted to pay less. That move is credited with lifting league TV revenue, and every owner benefits from a bigger pot, Dallas included.Then came buildings. AT&T Stadium, a billion-dollar venue in Arlington, turned game days into an events business. In 2008 he teamed with Yankee Global Enterprises to start Legends Hospitality, which runs food, drink, merchandise and operations at venues such as Cowboys Stadium.Land is the quieter play. His real estate firm, Blue Star Land, paid $38 million in 2018 for a 200-acre site that became Star Business Park. It added another 60 acres in 2019. Part of that ground is planned for a 400,000-square-foot merchandise and distribution center for the team.Each piece feeds the next. The stadium draws crowds, Legends serves them, and the land captures what grows around it. That is why his wealth is not simply a bet on the scoreboard.Where the rest of his money comes fromJones was a deal maker long before he owned a team. In the 1960s he borrowed $1 million from the Teamsters to open Shakey's Pizza restaurants in Missouri. The venture failed. He then worked at his father's insurance firm, returned to Arkansas for a business master's degree in 1970 and launched Jones Oil and Land Lease. Forbes says he earned his first million in 1970s oil investments, and he still backs drilling plus retail and residential real estate around Dallas. Wealth trackers also link him to Comstock Resources, a natural gas producer.Some of it is spent in plain sight. Forbes reported a cost of about $250 million for his 357-foot superyacht, though other coverage puts it nearer $225 million. His Highland Park home in Dallas is valued around $20 million.The family business is also the family. Stephen is chief operating officer and handles player personnel. Charlotte oversees charities and special events. Jerry Jr. leads sales and marketing. Jones gave all three limited partnership interests in the early 1990s, so the succession plan has been moving for decades.At 84, Jones still holds the owner, president and general manager roles. Only one other NFL owner, Mike Brown of the Bengals, runs football operations in a similar way.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Miami Hurricanes Ranked Best Transfer Portal Quarterback Destination
articles.summary: From Cam Ward’s Heisman run to Carson Beck’s resurgence, Miami Hurricanes' Mario Cristobal has turned Coral Gables into an elite launchpad for veteran passer...
articles.body:
The No. 1 Miami Hurricanes were ranked the top destination for transfer-portal quarterbacks, according to On3, and it should be a no-brainer at this point.

Coral Gables has been home to three high-caliber passers, two of whom capitalized on the opportunity, and one is currently carving out a similar path.

It started ahead of the 2024 season and head coach Mario Cristobal needed a proven quarterback. He landed Cam Ward from Washington State and it became the start of a recent trend. The Heisman Trophy finalist completed 305 of 454 passes (67.2 percent) while throwing for 4,313 yards and 39 touchdowns.

Ward received consensus All-American honors and became the No. 1 pick, selected by the Tennessee Titans, in the 2025 NFL Draft. After he departed, Carson Beck joined the Coral Gables program.

It was a unique situation, as the Jacksonville (Fla.) native had spent the previous five seasons at Georgia. In the 2024 Southeastern Conference championship game, Beck suffered a right elbow injury, which ended up being a UCL tear. He initially declared for the NFL Draft, same class as Ward, but decided to change course.

Given the injury, Beck's future in football was uncertain. He took advantage of the opportunity to return to college football and reinvent himself. Rather than going back to familiar territory in Athens (GA), Beck returned to the Sunshine State.

There were concerns about whether the sixth-year veteran could propel the Hurricanes back to former glory. He led them to a 5-0 start to the 2025 season, but two losses against Louisville and SMU put all hopes in jeopardy. As Beck's arm returned to full strength, it led the Hurricanes to a dominant four-game win streak to close the regular season, which was enough to make the College Football Playoffs through an at-large bid.

After beating Texas A&M, Ohio State (former reigning champions), and Ole Miss, "The U" had returned to the National Championship for the first time since 2003. Despite falling short against Indiana, Beck's football future found new life, and was taken in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft, selected by the Arizona Cardinals.

In search of another transfer-portal quarterback, the Hurricanes fell short of a few candidates, including Sam Leavitt, Brendan Sorsby, and Ty Simpson. Right before the window closed, Darian Mensah answered the call. The previous Atlantic Coast Conference leader in passing yards (3,973 yards) and touchdowns (34) kept the Hurricanes' National Championship hopes alive, currently 7-0 (ACC 5-0) this season and leading the Football Bowl Subdivision with an 81.4 completion percentage.

Mensah will likely be another one-and-done situation, like Ward and Beck, despite having extra NCAA eligibility remaining. If he remains projected as a high first-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, the chances of him staying in Coral Gables are slim. Although the Hurricanes will look to give the young quarterback core, such as Luke Nickel and Dereon Coleman, a chance to lead the offense, it doesn't guarantee that a proven transfer won't step foot on campus.

Given the proven track record, it's difficult for potential candidate to ignore. The spring portal window starts on Jan. 4, 2027 to Jan. 13.

articles.title: 6 NFL Teams That Should Follow Bears by Trading 2027 1st-Round Picks at the 2026 Deadline
articles.summary: On Thursday, the Chicago Bears pulled off the first true blockbuster trade of the 2026 NFL season. While notable veterans Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner were dealt earlier in the week, Chicago's acquisition of star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons felt like the sort of move that could shift the Super Bowl race.
articles.body:
On Thursday, the Chicago Bears pulled off the first true blockbuster trade of the 2026 NFL season. While notable veterans Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner were dealt earlier in the week, Chicago's acquisition of star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons felt like the sort of move that could shift the Super Bowl race.

Simmons is a four-time Pro Bowler and an elite defender still in his prime. He'll have a dramatic impact on the Bears' defense, though landing him was pricey. Chicago surrendered first-round picks in 2027 and 2028, plus a 2027 fourth-rounder, for Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick.

It was a very aggressive move by the Bears, one that could open the floodgates for more blockbusters before the November 10 trade deadline.

"All hell is going to break loose over the next week and a half," one unnamed source told NFL insider Jordan Schultz . " Get your popcorn ready."

While not every franchise is poised to chase the Super Bowl this season, for a few select teams, following Chicago's lead and trading premium draft capital for immediate talent would make sense.

The Buffalo Bills sit at 5-1 and hold the top spot in Bleacher Report's latest power rankings . They already have the look and feel of a Super Bowl favorite, though that has a lot to do with the presence of quarterback Josh Allen.

Buffalo's 31st-ranked defense could use some help.

Specifically, the Bills could use a playmaking cornerback or safety who can generate turnovers. Buffalo has recorded just three interceptions on the season while ranking 26th in net yards per pass attempt allowed.

According to Sports Illustrated 's Albert Breer , the Bills "are looking for another piece or two on defense."

To be fair, there probably isn't an available defensive back who is worth a first-round pick and who would fit into Buffalo's cap constraints. However, that shouldn't stop GM Brandon Beane from taking a bold swing at a star on a rookie deal like Cooper DeJean or Quinyon Mitchell.

Defensive backs like Riq Woolen, Budda Baker, and Donte Jackson are more realistic targets for Buffalo, if Beane can generate the cap space.

Alternatively, the Bills could boost their pass defense by improving a pass rush that has logged just 11 sacks so far. Maxx Crosby would be an obvious target if Beane can juggle the salary cap, while edge-rushers like Khalil Mack, Will McDonald IV, Jermaine Johnson II, and Josh Sweat should also be on Buffalo's radar.

In years past, putting the Cincinnati Bengals in the conversation of deadline buyers would be laughable. However, the traditionally thrifty franchise appears to have turned over a new and aggressive leaf in 2026.

Cincinnati made the ambitious decision to trade the 10th overall pick for defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence in the spring.

The Bengals' new-look defense hasn't been dominant but ranks eighth in points allowed. Quarterback Joe Burrow is healthy, and Cincinnati is keeping pace in the talented AFC North at 4-2. With an open playoff window, it's time for the Bengals to stay aggressive and add that missing piece.

Cincinnati's only glaring need right now is at running back. While Chase Brown has been a very capable starter in the past, he's currently averaging just 3.5 yards per carry and hasn't logged a run longer than 13 yards. As a team, Cincinnati ranks 28th in yards per carry.

Jonathan Taylor looms as the most obvious trade target. However, the Bengals might also check in on New York Jets running back Breece Hall, given the recent production of backup Braelon Allen. Though he isn't currently healthy, Saquon Barkley might be an option if Cincinnati truly wants to be aggressive.

Tony Pollard is an impending 2027 free agent and another back who could potentially be had.

The last time the Bengals had an above-average defense and a fully healthy Burrow, they reached the AFC title game. However, they've never been able to pair those two assets with an elite rushing attack. Now is the time to make it happen.

Jacksonville Jaguars general manager James Gladstone is no stranger to making aggressive moves. He moved up for receiver/cornerback Travis Hunter in the 2025 draft, and he dealt starting corner Tyson Campbell for Greg Newsome II before last year's deadline.

It's time for Gladstone and the Jaguars to make another bold move. Jacksonville currently controls the AFC South at 4-2, and Liam Coen's squad is one of the better teams in the AFC. However, it may fall a bit short of being Super Bowl-caliber.

Jacksonville's biggest issue is that, even with Hunter starting to play well as a cornerback, the secondary has been a liability. The Jags rank 29th in net yards per pass attempt allowed and 30th in passing yards allowed. That could be a massive problem against quarterbacks like Allen, Burrow, and Patrick Mahomes in the playoffs.

DeJean and Mitchell would be bold targets for Jacksonville, but Gladstone should be taking big swings. He would have to clear cap space to do it, but Gladstone might also want to see if the rival Indianapolis Colts are willing to cut their losses with Sauce Gardner now that the franchise is in fire-sale mode.

One way or another, the Jags need to improve their cornerback group, and the bigger the talent, the better.

Jacksonville should also afford to improve a pass rush that has recorded just 10 sacks through six games. With Travon Walker and Josh Hines-Allen already on the roster, it might make the most sense to chase an interior rusher like Moro Ojomo or Zach Sieler.

Almost all of the pieces are in place for the Kansas City Chiefs to vault back into the Super Bowl.

Steve Spagnuolo's defense ranks second in points allowed. Patrick Mahomes is healthy, and Kenneth Walker III has given Andy Reid a top-tier ground game with which to work. The Chiefs were undefeated before last week's blowout loss against the Seattle Seahawks.

However, that loss revealed a truth about Kansas City's offense in 2026. When defenses can shut down Walker, Mahomes can struggle. This is because the Chiefs lack viable playmakers at wide receiver.

Yes, the absence of Rashee Rice (hamstring) played a role in Kansas City's disappointing Week 7 performance, but the Chiefs could use receiver help even with Rice in the lineup. Reportedly, they are looking for it.

According to Breer , the Chiefs are looking at wide receivers ahead of the deadline.

GM Brett Veach is extremely limited on cap space, so a receiver on a rookie deal like Brian Thomas Jr. would make the most sense for Kansas City. If he can do some shuffling, though, he should make a run at a veteran like Wilson, too. Ideally, Veach would find a long-term solution at receiver.

Josh Downs, Rashod Bateman, Marquise Brown, and Jauan Jennings are other receivers who should be on Kansas City's radar, though they wouldn't be worth anything close to a first-rounder.

The Minnesota Vikings are the league's last undefeated team, but they could use help to keep stacking wins and make a run at the Super Bowl.

Minnesota has a championship-caliber defense but has struggled with offensive efficiency and consistency. Underwhelming quarterback play—Kyler Murray holds a passer rating of just 85.8—has been the biggest issue. Of course, teams aren't exactly giving away starting-caliber quarterbacks in-season.

If general manager Nolan Teasley could pry Mac Jones away from the San Francisco 49ers, he'd have to consider it. However, San Francisco is unlikely to help a fellow NFC contender get better.

Assuming that coach Kevin O'Connell is happy with Murray's progress, boosting the ground game should be Minnesota's top priority. Aaron Jones has been dealing with an MCL sprain, and the Vikings rank just 22nd in yards per carry.

Taylor is an obvious candidate for Minnesota. He's a productive dual-threat who would help Murray in the passing game, and he has a home-run gear that Jones no longer possesses and Jordan Mason has never really had.

Taylor currently ranks seventh in the NFL with 765 scrimmage yards. He's tied for second with eight touchdowns. Barkley, Hall, and Pollard are other backs the Vikings could consider, though Taylor should remain priority No. 1.

The 49ers have already made one bold move by trading for Buckner. San Francisco got the talented defensive tackle for a fourth-round pick, and the move appeared to be GM John Lynch's answer to the Seahawks' acquisition of Nelson.

Lynch shouldn't make Buckner his final addition. The 6-1 49ers have a legitimate shot to get their first Lombardi Trophy under head coach Kyle Shanahan, but their window is closing. Players like Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle, Trent Williams, and Mike Evans are great, but they're getting older.

The Seahawks, meanwhile, are the defending champ, and the Los Angeles Rams have a roster that, on paper, is as good as any in the league. If San Francisco wants to win the NFC West and go get that Super Bowl ring, it should continue being aggressive.

Really, there's little reason not to be. The 49ers have cap space to spare, which makes just about every potential trade target reasonably realistic.

Lynch should consider taking a big swing at a pass-rusher like Crosby to boost the pass rush. The defense will eventually have Nick Bosa back, but it has recorded just 15 sacks this season after recording just 20 all of last season. Edge-defenders like Mack and Sweat would make sense, too, if Lynch isn't willing to part with a first-round pick.

The 49ers could also use receiver help, given the injuries of Evans and Deebo Samuel—and given their age. A receiver like Wilson could be a great long-term addition in San Francisco.

*Cap information from Spotrac . Current draft order from Tankathon .

articles.title: Colts now 'open' to Jonathan Taylor trade with multiple teams in contact. Are Vikings among them?
articles.summary: ESPN's Adam Schefter reported the change of tune from Indianapolis.
articles.body:
After insisting he's not for sale for several days, the Indianapolis Colts are reportedly now willing to part with star running back Jonathan Taylor, a player with whom the Minnesota Vikings have been linked.

ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Saturday morning that the Colts are now open to trading Taylor, and that "multiple teams have reached out to Indianapolis."

"Those talks are said to be active and ongoing, according to sources," Schefter adds.

Speculation has been rife over the past week that running back is one of the areas the Minnesota Vikings could look to for a trade in an effort to boost their stuttering offense, and Taylor would be a star addition that adds a whole new dimension to the attack.

The ESPN report cites the Vikings as one of five teams that are thought to have expressed some interest in Taylor, with the others being the Denver Broncos, Green Bay Packers, Seattle Seahawks, and the New York Giants.

But there have also been rumblings that the Vikings are not willing to part with significant draft assets for the position, with NFL insider Tom Pelissero identifying running back as a need, but said fans shouldn't hold their breath for a trade bringing in the likes of Taylor or Saquon Barkley.

The buzz on Friday was that Vikings GM Nolan Teasley has been "working the phones like a madman," suggesting the Vikings are very much trying to make something happen to boost their 6-0 team.

However, SI's Albert Breer said interior offensive and defensive linemen were also areas where the Vikings are looking to strengthen, so it remains to be seen how much draft capital the Vikings are willing to give up.

It's been thought this week that the Colts were looking for a first-round pick for Taylor, something the Vikings almost certainly wouldn't part with given they may very well need a quarterback come the end of the season. Breer on Saturday said that the Colts will be looking for a "significant haul" for Taylor.

But ESPN's Jeremy Fowler believes that a second round pick "and more" – likely one or more later-round picks – will get the deal done.

The Vikings have accrued additional third- and fifth-round picks for the 2027 NFL Draft after trading Jonathan Greenard and J.J. McCarthy.

The Kansas Chiefs announced an unfortunate update on Travis Kelce on Thursday. However, the team released good news the following day about the veteran tight end's practice participation, just two days before its showdown with the Denver Broncos.

articles.title: Travis Kelce bought his first home for under $1M and his second for $6M in cash; the strategy behind every move
articles.summary: Travis Kelce paid $995,000 for his first Kansas City home in 2019.
articles.body: Travis Kelce paid $995,000 for his first Kansas City home in 2019. Four years later, he bought a gated estate in Leawood, Kansas, for just under $6 million, and Robb Report says he paid in cash. TMZ reported the deal closed in October 2023, about a month after Taylor Swift attended her first Chiefs game. The sequence is simple. Kelce kept his early purchase modest, stayed put for years, and upgraded only when the attention outside his front door made the old place hard to live in.Travis Kelce's first home and the $6 million cash purchaseThe first house sat in Briarcliff West, a Kansas City neighborhood. It was a custom-built, seven-bedroom property, and Kelce bought it in 2019. That same year, he, his brother Jason and their mother Donna put $355,000 into an Orlando condo. Reports disagree on the size of the Briarcliff house, with some saying 4,200 square feet and others 10,000.The second purchase was a different scale.The Leawood property sits on a little over three acres and was built in 1998. According to the Kansas City Journal, it previously belonged to a prominent medical malpractice attorney in the area. The price came in just under $6 million. The cash detail traces back to Robb Report, so it is best read as reported rather than confirmed by the buyer.Privacy drove the upgradeThe timing is hard to ignore. Swift went to Kelce's September 24 game against the Bears, and within three days Kelce told Jason that photographers had started showing up at his house. TMZ's sources called the old place far too accessible. Still, talk of Kelce leaving Briarcliff had been circulating for months before Swift appeared, so the relationship likely sped up a move that was already on the table.The new address solves the problem. It is a gated community, the house sits in a cul-de-sac, and Arrowhead Stadium is about 20 minutes away.The grounds include a pool with a waterfall, a tennis and pickleball court and a mini golf course. Reports put the house at six bedrooms and six bathrooms. The lower level has a wine cellar, a gym with a sauna, a club room with a full bar and kitchen, and a six-car garage. Nearly everything a player might want on a day off is already behind the gate, which was the point.What the money behind it looks likeKelce signed a reported $57.25 million extension with the Chiefs in 2022. That works out to about $14.3 million a year through the 2026 season. HELLO! Magazine put his net worth near $50 million in early 2024. Measured against that figure, the first house was about 2 percent of his wealth and the Leawood estate roughly 12 percent. Neither one is reckless.Cash makes the math cleaner still. If he did pay outright, there is no mortgage to carry, no interest compounding in the background and no lender asking questions about future income. That matters for an athlete whose earning window has a clear end date. EssentiallySports now lists his 2026 deal at one year and $12 million, fully guaranteed. It is a drop from the old annual number, and owning the house free and clear makes that drop easier to absorb.There is also the Briarcliff house, which HELLO! Magazine estimated at just over $1 million in early 2024. Kelce held it as a roughly break-even asset instead of dumping it fast. The pattern holds across both deals: buy at a price he can cover easily, wait, and move only when something forces the issue.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
