articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Surprise Jeffery Simmons Suitors Before Blockbuster Trade to Bears from Titans
articles.summary: Before the Chicago Bears pulled off the biggest blockbuster of the trade-deadline season so far, there were other playoff contenders that made calls to the Tennessee Titans for Jeffery Simmons.
articles.body:
Before the Chicago Bears pulled off the biggest blockbuster of the trade-deadline season so far, there were other playoff contenders that made calls to the Tennessee Titans for Jeffery Simmons.

Per The Athletic's Jonathan Jones , New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh called Strunk "directly" in an attempt to trade for Simmons:

"The Giants have been looking to make a deal ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline, knowing they will go into Week 9 atop the NFC East. General manager Joe Schoen had previously reached out to Titans GM Mike Borgonzi, who told Schoen and other inquiring teams that they wouldn't trade Simmons.

"Harbaugh then opted to call Strunk, the Titans' controlling owner, in an attempt to get Simmons. Harbaugh got the same message from Strunk, who has empowered Borgonzi to make football decisions for the franchise."

The Ringer's Tom Pelissero added at least three teams spoke to the Titans about Simmons, including the Jacksonville Jaguars.

It's unclear how far any talks between Tennessee and Jacksonville went because Pelissero noted the Titans probably viewed it as a "nonstarter" to trade Simmons within their division, but Jaguars general manager James Gladstone making the call "probably portends more activity" for them leading up to the deadline.

Jones cited one NFL general manager who felt Harbaugh calling the owner of another team as violating a "code amongst primary football decision-makers" in that they only deal with each other.

There is a bit of an established relationship between Harbaugh and Strunk. He was scheduled to interview with Titans officials, including Strunk and general manager Mike Borgonzi, at his home in January.

The meeting never took place because Harbaugh was hired by the Giants right before Strunk and Borgonzi were getting ready to fly out, per Sports Illustrated 's Albert Breer .

One reason the Giants were unable to pull off the trade for Simmons is their lack of available draft capital. They don't currently own a fourth- or fifth-round pick in 2027.

New York could add a fourth-rounder based on the comp pick formula after Wan'Dale Robinson signed with the Titans in the offseason, but compensatory picks can't be traded until after they have been awarded.

The Bears' trade package for Simmons was headlined by two first-round picks in 2027 and 2028, but they also included a fourth-round selection in 2027.

It's also notable the Giants were trying to trade for a defensive tackle after sending Dexter Lawrence to the Cincinnati Bengals in the offseason.

The defensive-tackle market is thinning out leading up to the Nov. 10 trade deadline with Simmons and DeForest Buckner, who was traded to the San Francisco 49ers, already being moved.

Despite their need for help on the interior of the defensive line, the Giants are sitting in a good position right now with a 4-2-1 record that has them in first place in the NFC East going into their bye in Week 8.

While Patrick Mahomes is busy gearing up for the Week 7 clash against the Denver Broncos, Brittany Mahomes has recently celebrated a milestone they achieved in Kansas City.Patrick Mahomes' wife Brittany Mahomes makes another impact in Kansas City’s community ahead of Week 7 clashA few hours ago, Joe's Kansas City Bar-B-Que made a post on social media announcing that it has become the first local restaurant recognized through the 15 and FARE program.The post read as, "We are really proud today to post this sign up," the post's caption read. "Joe's is the first restaurant to be recognized as 15 & Fare approved. Over the past two years our management staff in our restaurants have become certified in food allergy prep & handling."The post added, "This initiative was started by @patrickmahomes & @brittanylynne and their charity @15andMahomies. Now we want others to join us! We'll be sharing soon how other restaurants can join 15 & Fare!"To this, Patrick Mahomes’ wife, the popular entrepreneur Brittany Mahomes responded as, "👏🏼👏🏼👏🏼👏🏼”.For the unversed, Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ foundation, 15 and the Mahomies collaborated with FARE (Food Allergy Research & Education in 2024 to help Kansas City area restaurants better serve customers with food allergies.According to this project, the Kansas City restaurants must train at least 90% of their food-service staff, complete monthly on-site audits for three consecutive months, maintain a written food allergy management policy and provide allergen information on their menus.Patrick Mahomes’ wife Brittany Mahomes reflects on how scary it was dealing with their children's allergiesPatrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ oldest children have food allergies that served as an inspiration behind this noble project.In an interview with Kids With Food Allergies, Brittany Mahomes opened up about it as she said, “I think as a mom of two kids that do have food allergies, I think it's important to raise awareness of this and get the information out there. articles.title: Micah Parsons Injury Update, Latest NFL Rumors on Timeline for Packers Star's 2026 Debut
articles.summary: Having won four of their last five games, the Green Bay Packers are going to get reinforcements for the stretch run with Micah Parsons eyeing a return in late-November.
articles.body:
Having won four of their last five games, the Green Bay Packers are going to get reinforcements for the stretch run with Micah Parsons eyeing a return in late-November.

Per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network and ESPN, the Packers and Parsons have Nov. 25 against the Los Angeles Rams targeted for the five-time Pro Bowler to make his season debut.

Rapaport added the Packers are expected to open Parsons' practice window next week as he continues the ramp-up process in his rehab from a torn ACL.

Parsons originally tore the ACL in his left knee in Week 15 against the Denver Broncos last season.

While the Packers were mum throughout the offseason about his potential return date, Parsons said in August that Week 6 against the Dallas Cowboys was "very realistic" for his first appearance in 2026.

"Is it possible? Yes, so I wouldn't say it's not possible. At the same time, in the next 10, 12 weeks from now, we've got to make it possible by putting the work in," Parsons added.

After Week 6 came and went with Parsons still on the physically unable to perform list, his timeline remained up in the air.

ESPN's Rob Demovsky noted on Thursday the Packers have historically taken a cautious approach with players coming this type of injury and they "almost never put a player recovering from a torn ACL on the practice field until nine months after the date of surgery."

A return to practice next week would mark just over 10 months since Parsons had surgery to repair his ACL. It also gives the Packers a 21-day window to get him up to game speed before they have to put him on the 53-man roster or he will miss the remainder of the season.

The Packers-Rams matchup at SoFi Stadium is the NFL's first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game. It will also come after Green Bay's bye in Week 11, giving Parsons extra recovery time before and after the game assuming he does end up playing.

Despite being one of four NFC teams with at least five wins so far this season, the Packers are currently in last place in their own division. They are behind the undefeated Minnesota Vikings, Chicago Bears (5-2) and Detroit Lions (4-2) in the NFC North.

Parsons' return will provide a huge boost to a Packers defense that already leads the NFL with 22 sacks. He has recorded at least 12 sacks in each of his first five seasons, including 12.5 in 13 games last year.

articles.title: "It means a lot not only to myself as a single mother": How Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes bring holiday cheer to Kansas City families with a heartwarming move
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes brought some holiday cheer to Kansas City families in December 2023.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes brought some holiday cheer to Kansas City families in December 2023. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback stepped away from the football field to spend time with children at EarlyStart's Clothing Kits for Kids drive. But the visit offered more than a chance to meet one of the NFL's biggest stars. Mahomes and his foundation helped families get essential winter clothing, including coats, socks, hats and gloves.The event took place on Wednesday, December 20, just days before Christmas. Mahomes' foundation, 15 and the Mahomies, donated dozens of winter clothing items for the drive. By the end of the event, 124 clothing kits had reached families. For parents dealing with everyday expenses, the support meant a little less worry during the colder months. One mother, Nataliya Shalib, explained why the visit meant so much to her and her son.Patrick Mahomes and Brittany help 124 Kansas City families with winter clothingMahomes and Brittany joined EarlyStart's students and their families for the holiday event. Their visit gave the children an opportunity to meet the Chiefs quarterback while also receiving clothing they could use throughout winter.The donation came through 15 and the Mahomies, Mahomes' charitable foundation. The kits included coats, socks, hats and gloves. These were basic items, but they could make a real difference for families who struggled to afford winter essentials.June McDaniel, EarlyStart's interim CEO, explained the need during an interview with KSHB 41 reporter Rae Daniel at the December 20 clothing drive."They're getting coats and socks and hats a gloves and all these things are essential in order for them to get through the winter months," McDaniel said.She also spoke about her own understanding of the challenges some families face. McDaniel said some children arrive at school without knowing where their next meal will come from or whether they will have a warm coat the following day."I would've wanted what we're providing today, which is love and care and support," she added.Her comments showed why the drive went beyond a holiday celebration. For EarlyStart, providing these essentials also meant helping children feel comfortable and supported as they continued their education. Young fan RJ gives Patrick Mahomes a heartwarming momentWhile the clothing kits helped families, one small moment between Mahomes and a young student gave the event an especially personal touch.Nataliya Shalib attended the drive with her son RJ, who received a green coat. Excited about his new winter clothing, RJ wanted to make sure the Chiefs quarterback noticed it."Hey Patrick! Look at my new coat," RJ called out to Mahomes during the December 20 event, as reported by KSHB.His excitement reflected what the visit meant to the children. They did not just receive winter clothing. They also got to spend time with a player they admired.For Shalib, meeting Mahomes and Brittany was equally meaningful. She spoke about how the couple's support extended beyond major businesses and reached children, schools and families who needed help."He doesn't just think about just big businesses, he thinks about the kids, the schools, you know - families especially during the holidays. It definitely means a lot," she told KSHB.The mother also highlighted how much the donation meant to single parents in the community."It means a lot not only myself as a single mother, but single mothers and fathers here too. As she put it during the event, "You're not in this alone. articles.title: Colts reportedly open to trading RB Jonathan Taylor before Nov. 10 deadline
articles.summary: Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner were already moved this week. Could Taylor be the next to go?
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts are open to trading running back Jonathan Taylor, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .

After a week where the 2-5 Colts began a fire sale by moving guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner , while also being told by wide receiver Josh Downs that he would like to be trade d , Taylor could be the biggest transaction made by interim general manager Ed Dodds ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

Taylor said this week that he met with Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon to talk about his future with the team. While the team originally wanted to keep the 27-year-old running back as part of its rebuild, that sentiment has apparently changed, especially knowing the type of return the three-time Pro Bowler could deliver.

Speaking to reporters on Thursday, Taylor confirmed that he did not request a trade, but understood that he isn't in control of the situation.

"I'm proud to wear the horseshoe, proud to be here. Similar to Quenton [Nelson] and [DeForest Buckner], they were proud to wear the horseshoe, they were proud to be here," Taylor said. "But obviously, circumstances may cause otherwise. Hopefully that day may not come, but I can't control that."

There are already a number of suitors interested in acquiring Taylor. According to Schefter and Rapoport, the Denver Broncos, Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings, New York Giants and Seattle Seahawks are among the teams who have inquired.

The Colts would reportedly be looking for a futures-heavy return in a trade, much like the four draft picks that the Carolina Panthers acquired in 2022 when they moved running back Christian McCaffrey to the San Francisco 49ers.

By trading Nelson and Buckner, the Colts gained third- and fourth-round draft picks in 2027 and a fifth-rounder in 2028. They currently do not own a 2027 first-rounder as that went to the New York Jets in the Sauce Gardner trade.

Taylor signed a two-year, $44 millon extension in August with $39 million in guaranteed money. The extension runs through the 2028 season with his salary cap hit at $16.2 million this season, $21 million in 2027 and just under $23 million in 2028, according to Over the Cap .

There is no word if the Colts will sit Taylor out for their Week 8 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars for asset protection. Despite his trade request, Downs will play on Sunday after head coach Shane Steichen told him , "You've got to show up and we gotta go play a game on Sunday."

Taylor has rushed for at least 1,100 yards in four of his six NFL seasons and has just under 600 yards through seven games this season.

articles.title: “Can’t get too much worse”: Shilo Sanders eyes New York move after rejecting expensive Florida homes amid $11.89 million bankruptcy fight
articles.summary: Shilo Sanders may have another city on his house-hunting list.
articles.body: Shilo Sanders may have another city on his house-hunting list. After weeks of checking out expensive properties across South Florida, Deion Sanders’ son is now considering New York. The former Colorado safety recently revealed his plans during a YouTube video, and the city's high living costs do not seem to have scared him away.When a New Yorker warned him about the prices, Shilo had a rather casual response. He has already had his share of expensive property tours in Florida. However, his search for a new home comes while he continues to fight an $11.89 million judgment in bankruptcy court. Shilo Sanders wants to check out New York after turning down Miami rentalsShilo made his New York plans clear in a YouTube video on his channel while spending time in West Palm Beach. During a conversation with a man from New York, he revealed that he wanted to visit the city and look at properties.“I’m actually going to go out there and do a house hunt video there ’cause I’m trying to look in New York. Should I move there?” Shilo asked.The man immediately warned him about the city's expensive lifestyle. But Shilo was not ready to back away from the idea.“That’s fine, bro. Yeah, I already live here. It can’t get too much worse than this,” he replied.The conversation then moved to taxes, food and the city's 24-hour lifestyle. The New Yorker pointed out that having something to do at any hour was one of the biggest attractions of living there.However, New York is not the first place Shilo has considered. He has spent several weeks looking at properties in Florida, particularly Miami and Fort Lauderdale. Some of those tours did not go as planned.During his recent house hunt, Shilo checked out rentals priced at $14,000, $11,000 and just under $10,000 per month. One Miami property caught his attention because of its river views and downtown location. But the $14,000 monthly rent quickly ended his interest.He also made it clear that he was tired of the prices during another property search.“I ain’t going to keep playing around with these Miami prices, bro, and I’m going to Texas,” he said in one of his house-hunting videos.His younger brother, Shedeur Sanders, even offered to help with a down payment. Shilo joked that if Shedeur bought him a house, it would probably cost at least $2 million. He has also mentioned that around $6,000 would be his preferred monthly price range. Shilo Sanders house hunt continues while $11.89 million bankruptcy case awaits rulingWhile Shilo looks at his next home, his financial situation remains under scrutiny in court. The 26-year-old is still fighting to discharge an $11.89 million judgment awarded to former high school security guard John Darjean.The dispute goes back to September 17, 2015, when Shilo was 15. He got into an altercation with Darjean at his school in Dallas. Darjean later sued him over injuries he said he suffered during the incident. Shilo did not appear at the 2022 civil trial, and the court entered a default judgment of $11,890,937 against him.In October 2023, Shilo filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy. He wants the judgment discharged, but Darjean argues that the injuries resulted from a willful and malicious act. That distinction could determine whether bankruptcy law allows Shilo to erase the debt.The two sides presented their arguments during a five-day trial in Denver from August 31 to September 4, 2026. Shilo maintained that he acted in self-defense. Judge Michael Romero also raised concerns about missing surveillance footage during the proceedings.“It just appears real obvious that there is some missing video that no one seems to have been able to find,” Romero said during the bankruptcy trial.The judge has yet to issue a ruling. Following a delay in the submission of post-trial briefs, the deadline for final written arguments moved from November 16 to December 21, 2026. A decision is now expected in January 2027 or later.As of now, Shilo has another property search on his mind. After turning down several expensive Florida rentals, he could soon take his search to New York. Whether he finds a home there or decides to return to Texas, his next move remains one to watch.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: New 49ers Rumors on Potential WR Trade After DeForest Buckner Deal Ahead of 2026 NFL Deadline
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers reportedly may be looking to make yet another splash ahead of the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers reportedly may be looking to make yet another splash ahead of the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline.

According to Jonathan Jones of The Athletic, the Niners are "sniffing around" for wide receiver help, as they deal with numerous injuries at the position.

The 49ers have already made one significant trade, acquiring three-time Pro Bowl and one-time First Team All-Pro defensive tackle DeForest Buckner from the Indianapolis Colts this week.

While that move fortified San Francisco's front four on defense, there is no question that wideout remains a need offensively.

Ricky Pearsall, Demarcus Robinson and rookie De'Zhaun Stribling are all on injured reserve, while Deebo Samuel has missed the past two games with a hamstring injury, and Mike Evans missed last week's game against the Atlanta Falcons with rib and Achilles ailments.

The Niners suffered their first loss of the season last week, falling 29-20 to the Falcons on the road.

A lack of production from the wide receiver position seemed to play a significant role in the loss.

Tight end George Kittle led San Francisco with 88 receiving yards, followed by running back Christian McCaffrey with 61 yards.

Outside of them, Jordan Watkins had three catches for 56 yards, Jacob Cowing had three grabs for 38 yards and Brandin Cooks made one reception for 13 yards.

Watkins, Cowing, Cooks and Christian Kirk are the only healthy wide receivers on San Francisco's roster currently, which is not a group that puts quarterback Brock Purdy in the best position to succeed.

Of course, Evans and Samuel should be back in the not-too-distant future, and Stribling should come off IR at some point as well.

However, in the meantime, Purdy and the San Francisco offense as a whole would benefit from a reliable receiver who can command at least some defensive attention.

Brian Thomas Jr. of the Jacksonville Jaguars, Jerry Jeudy of the Cleveland Browns, Josh Downs of the Indianapolis Colts, Jauan Jennings of the Minnesota Vikings, Chris Godwin of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Rashod Bateman of the Baltimore Ravens and Quentin Johnston of the Los Angeles Chargers are among the wide receivers rumored and speculated to potentially be available via trade.

The 6-1 49ers are on the bye this week, meaning their only game left before the trade deadline will take place on Nov. 8 against the Las Vegas Raiders.

articles.title: Maxx Crosby Trade Rumors Updated by NFL Insider, Raiders Star's Stance on Potential Deal Revealed
articles.summary: After the failed offseason trade that would have sent him to the Baltimore Ravens, Maxx Crosby has no interest in leaving the Las Vegas Raiders even though they will likely do their due diligence leading up to the Nov. 10 trade deadline.
articles.body:
After the failed offseason trade that would have sent him to the Baltimore Ravens, Maxx Crosby has no interest in leaving the Las Vegas Raiders even though they will likely do their due diligence leading up to the Nov. 10 trade deadline.

Per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero , Crosby has "no desire" to leave Las Vegas and views the failed Ravens trade as a "sign" he is supposed to remain with the Raiders.

Despite Crosby's stance, Pelissero noted Raiders general manager John Spytek is "sure to get calls" from interested teams about the star defender that leaves "open the possibility of another blockbuster."

The Ravens originally agreed to send two first-round picks in 2026 and 2027 to Las Vegas for Crosby on March 6, but the deal was called off four days later when the Raiders announced Baltimore backed out.

Baltimore's medical staff reportedly did not pass Crosby on his physical coming off knee surgery in January to repair a torn meniscus and related issues to that part of his leg.

Any concerns about Crosby's ability have been unfounded so far this season. The 29-year-old has 16 quarterback hits, three tackles for loss and two sacks in seven starts.

Crosby is also playing at a high volume having been on the field for 87.5 percent of the Raiders' defensive snaps.

One big hurdle standing in the way of any trade is Crosby's salary and cap hit. Pelissero noted he is still owed roughly $18.3 million for the remainder of this season. His total cap hit for 2026 is $35.8 million.

Among current playoff contenders, the San Francisco 49ers, Detroit Lions and Denver Broncos are the only teams with at least $20 million in available cap space.

There is always a way to make the money work if a team wants to get a deal done, but it would likely require some financial maneuvering.

If the Raiders could find someone willing to offer a package similar to what they were planning on getting from Baltimore, it would seem to be difficult to pass up for a team that is starting to fall out of playoff contention coming off four straight losses after a surprise 3-0 start.

articles.title: Arch Manning Falls, Drew Mestemaker Rises in NFL Scouts' Poll of Top QB in 2027 Draft
articles.summary: NFL scouts and executives have cooled on Arch Manning and become enamored with Drew Mestemaker in analyzing the top quarterbacks eligible for the 2027 draft.
articles.body:
NFL scouts and executives have cooled on Arch Manning and become enamored with Drew Mestemaker in analyzing the top quarterbacks eligible for the 2027 draft.

In a survey of 25 league scouts and executives conducted by ESPN's Pete Thamel , Mestemaker is clearly viewed as the No. 1 quarterback in the upcoming class with 17 votes.

Notre Dame's CJ Carr (four votes), Miami's Darian Mensah (three) and Oregon's Dante Moore (one) split the remaining eight votes.

Manning, who was the No. 2 QB in Thamel's preseason survey from Sept. 12 with seven votes, received zero this time.

From the original survey, Thamel noted multiple scouts included Mestemaker among a group of quarterbacks who could play themselves into the first-round mix if they performed well.

Now, there appears to be very little doubt among this particular group that Mestemaker is the primary signal-caller to keep an eye on looking at the 2027 draft.

"Mestemaker seems like the only real choice at this point," one scout told Thamel.

In his first season with Oklahoma State after transferring from UNLV, Mestemaker has thrown for 2,326 yards and 20 touchdowns through seven games.

B/R's NFL scouting department ranked Mestemaker as the No. 7 quarterback in the upcoming draft on its most recent big board released on Sept. 22.

Mensah was at the top the class for B/R, earning plaudits for being the most accurate and most pro-ready quarterback in the group.

Manning's on-field play has not yet hit the level that his raw talent suggests he can reach. He has thrown as many interceptions in seven games this season as he did in 13 games last year (seven).

The timing of Manning's turnovers is amplifying his struggles. Three of his last four interceptions came in the fourth quarter, including two against Oklahoma that led to 10 points in a 27-24 Texas loss.

Despite some of those issues for Manning, Thamel did note multiple scouts believe he could still end up being a first-round pick thanks to his "tools, pedigree and potential."

It's also going to be interesting to see how the 2027 quarterback class looks when all is said and done.

Manning and Moore, who is likely to miss the remainder of the season due to a concussion, still have college eligibility remaining. Neither player has indicated at this point what they plan to do.

The tentative deadline for underclassmen to declare for the 2027 draft is Jan. 13.

articles.title: Daniel Jones' Potential Colts Benching Discussed in New NFL Rumors After Buckner, Nelson Trades
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts are planning to stick with Daniel Jones for now after selling off multiple key players ahead of the trade deadline, NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported Saturday.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts are planning to stick with Daniel Jones for now after selling off multiple key players ahead of the trade deadline, NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported Saturday.

The Colts "haven't discussed benching" Jones after a 2-5 start led to the franchise trading Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, Pelissero reported on his Substack.

Pelissero noted injuries to Jones' receiving corps, as well as the lingering impact of the Achilles tendon the quarterback tore last December, could factor into the Colts' evaluation of his play.

Jones received the transition tag before he re-signed in Indianapolis this offseason on a two-year, $88 million deal. General manager Chris Ballard, who negotiated the contract, was fired earlier this month.

That deal includes $10.51 million in injury-guaranteed 2027 salary, which becomes fully guaranteed as of the fifth day of the next league year, per Spotrac . Pelissero noted that date "could factor into the Colts' thinking about making a change if and when they're eliminated from playoff contention."

Jones suffered a season-ending torn Achilles last December and made his return to the field just 280 days later.

He has been playing most of the season without wideout Alec Pierce and tight end Tyler Warren, although Warren has been cleared to play ahead of Sunday's divisional matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

The quarterback has completed 59.6 percent of his passes through his first seven games of the season while throwing for 1,398 receiving yards with four touchdowns and seven interceptions.

Jones was most recently held to 108 yards with no touchdowns and a game-ending interception in last Sunday's 16-10 loss at the Minnesota Vikings.

Colts head coach Shane Steichen said after that loss Jones was the team's "starting quarterback right now."

"We've got to be able to throw the ball better," Steichen said Monday, before adding he has faith in Jones to improve going forward.

"He's proven that he can do it. We've all seen it," Steichen said. "We've got to go do it, though. He's got to play better moving forward, and he'll tell you that himself, but I haven't lost that confidence in him."

The Colts made two major moves later that week by trading Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers in exchange for a total of three draft picks.

Jones acknowledged after the trades it was "natural to have some of those thoughts" wondering about his future in Indianapolis in the wake of Nelson and Buckner's departures (h/t The Athletic's James Boyd).

The Colts have Anthony Richardson Sr. and Riley Leonard waiting behind Jones on the depth chart should Steichen decide to make a quarterback change down the stretch.

Whether Jones is able to start turning things around Saturday in Jacksonville could impact both whether Richardson sees playing time this season and if the Colts decide to keep Jones on the roster past his March contract deadline.

articles.title: Philip Rivers, 8-time Pro Bowl QB, reportedly in serious talks about coaching alma mater NC State
articles.summary: Rivers famously paused his high school coaching career last year, when he returned to the NFL after close to five seasons without a snap in the league.
articles.body:
Last year, Philip Rivers shockingly came out of retirement and started three games for a quarterback-needy Indianapolis Colts team after close to five seasons without a snap in the NFL. This year, Rivers may return to the collegiate ranks — not to play, of course, but to coach his alma mater.

Rivers reportedly is in serious talks about coaching NC State, which moved on from longtime program frontman Dave Doeren last week.

The eight-time Pro Bowl QB has emerged as the focus of the Wolfpack's search for Doeren's long-term replacement, according to On3 . ESPN reported Saturday that, although Rivers hasn't met with NC State officials in person, there's been outreach about front-office construction, in case he agrees to take the job.

That said, the 44-year-old Rivers reportedly informed NC State that he wants to finish out the high school season in Alabama, where he's the head coach of Fairhope's St. Michael Catholic High School. And, per ESPN, a deal with the Wolfpack isn't close yet.

On Friday, following St. Michael's 53-32 loss to Foley High School, Rivers was asked about his name being linked to the NC State vacancy.

"I mean, shoot, NC State's special to me," Rivers said, via AL.com's Ben Thomas . "And you know, Coach Doeren, shoot, what he did over 14 years, and all-time winningest coach, [there's] a ton of respect and appreciation, you know, for how he went about it with the university. There's nothing there at this point. "Like I told you earlier in the week, you understand the chatter is out there. Gotta take it one day at a time, you know, is all I know. I'm excited [for] this postseason with these guys here, and I guess it's like I told you last year, you never say never, but there's nothing imminent."

"I mean, shoot, NC State's special to me," Rivers said, via AL.com's Ben Thomas . "And you know, Coach Doeren, shoot, what he did over 14 years, and all-time winningest coach, [there's] a ton of respect and appreciation, you know, for how he went about it with the university. There's nothing there at this point.

"Like I told you earlier in the week, you understand the chatter is out there. Gotta take it one day at a time, you know, is all I know. I'm excited [for] this postseason with these guys here, and I guess it's like I told you last year, you never say never, but there's nothing imminent."

While Rivers went 0-3 quarterbacking the Colts last season, his comeback was inspiring. He kept Indianapolis in games against three of the league's best: a 14-win Seattle Seahawks squad that went on to win the Super Bowl, a 12-win San Francisco 49ers group and a 13-win Jacksonville Jaguars team.

Rivers was piloting the offense as a literal grandfather . At the time he took over, he was older than 13 coaches leading NFL teams.

He was briefly in the running to join them last winter. In January, Rivers interviewed for the Buffalo Bills' job. Eventually, though, he removed himself from the search, per ESPN .

When asked Friday if his most recent stint in the NFL reignited his competitive fire for the next level, Rivers said he thinks it did, but when it comes to NC State, "that makes things a little bit different," he said, via Thomas .

Rivers authored an illustrious career at NC State, and one of his 10 children — Gunner Rivers, the 12th-highest rated QB in the 2027 class, according to the Rivals industry ranking — is currently committed to play there after graduating from St. Michael.

Before starring for the Chargers and Colts, Rivers thrived in Raleigh. He suited up for the Wolfpack from 2000-03 while establishing himself as a top-five pick. The 2002 Rivers-led NC State team won 11 games. In 2003, he threw for 4,491 yards and 34 touchdowns, completing 72% of his passes along the way.

At the moment, he's dialed in on helping St. Michael win a title. In his sixth season at the helm, Rivers has guided the Cardinals to the state playoff semifinals the last two years.

articles.title: NFL Exec Disputes Jaguars' Brian Thomas Jr. Trade Stance Amid Rumors At 2026 Deadline
articles.summary: Differing viewpoints have emerged regarding the likelihood of the Jacksonville Jaguars moving wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. before the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline.
articles.body:
Differing viewpoints have emerged regarding the likelihood of the Jacksonville Jaguars moving wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. before the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline.

According to Jonathan Jones of The Athletic, the Jags have been "fending off interest" in Thomas for the past year, and they "remain firm" in their desire to keep him.

However, an anonymous rival executive who was asked by Jones if they believe the Jaguars would part ways with BTJ said, "Yes they would."

Jones added that Thomas struggling and getting benched in the second half of the team's Week 6 loss to the Houston Texans "ramped up belief within the league that Jacksonville ultimately will move him by the deadline."

The 24-year-old Thomas was selected 23rd overall by the Jags in the 2024 NFL draft out of LSU.

Early indications suggested Thomas was a superstar in the making, as he earned Pro Bowl honors during his rookie season by recording 87 catches for 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns.

However, his production dropped sharply last season to the tune of 48 receptions for 707 yards and two touchdowns.

Thomas has bottomed out thus far in 2026, registering just nine grabs for 105 yards and one score through six games.

BTJ is clearly behind Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers in Jacksonville's wide receiver pecking order, and he has been supplanted by Josh Cameron and even Travis Hunter as of late also, despite Hunter primarily playing cornerback.

On top of that, quarterback Trevor Lawrence often looks in the direction of tight end Brenton Strange, who is tied for the team lead with 26 receptions.

Jones believes the Jaguars could get a Day 2 draft pick in exchange for Thomas, and if that is the case, then they may be wise to move him rather than continuing to bury him on the depth chart.

articles.title: New Titans Rumors on Tony Pollard, Calvin Ridley Trade Stances After Jeffery Simmons Deal With Bears

articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans are "more likely" to trade wide receiver Calvin Ridley than running back Tony Pollard, NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported Saturday on his Substack.

That likelihood is due to Ridley's position on the Titans' depth chart as well as "demand at the position," Pelissero reported.

The Titans started selling after falling to 1-6 ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline by dealing defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to the Chicago Bears in exchange for a package that included two first-round picks.

Pelissero reported "the Titans have shown no urgency to move Ridley," but that could change "with the ball rolling after the Simmons trade."

Pollard, 29, leads the Titans with 487 rushing yards in seven games this season as his team's biggest threat on the ground.

Ridley was seen as a candidate to be cut ahead of his age-31 season before he agreed to a restructured contract to stick around in Tennessee, per Pelissero . He has made just five catches for 81 yards in six games while Cam Ward has prioritized other targets including Carnell Tate, Wan'Dale Robinson and Elic Ayomanor.

Both players are potential trade targets because of their contract status. Pollard is playing on an expiring deal. Ridley is signed through 2027, but he could once more be a release candidate given his money past this season is not guaranteed.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler previously identified the Kansas City Chiefs and Pittsburgh Steelers as candidates to add a wideout ahead of the deadline.

articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Saints' Alvin Kamara Amid Trade Speculation From Teams at 2026 Deadline
articles.summary: Trade rumors and speculation are surrounding longtime New Orleans Saints running back Alvin Kamara ahead of the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline.
articles.body:
Trade rumors and speculation are surrounding longtime New Orleans Saints running back Alvin Kamara ahead of the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline.

According to Jonathan Jones of The Athletic, "multiple teams have mused" about Kamara's potential availability.

Kamara has long been resistant to playing elsewhere, and Jones referenced a quote from Kamara last season when he said, "If [general manager] Mickey [Loomis] comes down and says [they're trading me], I'm going to go drink a piña colada somewhere."

There was plenty of smoke around the idea of the Saints moving on from Kamara this past offseason, especially after signing running back Travis Etienne in free agency.

However, Kamara and the Saints renegotiated his deal , making it a one-year, $6 million pact for 2026.

With Etienne being limited to three games so far this season due to a hamstring injury that landed him on injured reserve, the 31-year-old Kamara has split time in the backfield with Kendre Miller.

Kamara is third on the team in rushing yardage (125) and tied for the team lead with two rushing touchdowns. He also leads Saints running backs with 22 receptions for 133 yards and one score.

New Orleans' running game has been virtually non-existent, though, as the Saints rank 27th in the NFL with 86 rushing yards per game.

Because of that and the reality of Etienne returning to the lineup at some point, perhaps it could make Kamara expendable.

While it is clear that Kamara is in the twilight of his career, he was once among the best and most complete running backs in the NFL.

A five-time Pro Bowler, Kamara has rushed for 7,375 yards and 63 touchdowns, along with catching 628 passes for 5,081 yards and 26 touchdowns over 10 NFL seasons.

Kamara finished with at least 1,100 yards from scrimmage in each of his first eight seasons, and he scored double-digit touchdowns in three of those seasons as well, including a league-leading 21 in 2020.

While Kamara is averaging just 3.0 yards per carry this season after averaging 3.6 last season, he is still an effective pass-catcher that could help a contending team.

The Saints don't seem like a contending team on the surface with a 2-5 record, but given how weak the NFC South is, they are just one game out of first place.

Because of that and Kamara's past unwillingness to go elsewhere, keeping Kamara in the fold may be the most likely scenario when the trade deadline arrives.

articles.title: Packers' Josh Jacobs was accused of abuse by 3 other women after May arrest, records show
articles.summary: Jacobs missed the first six weeks of the season and returned in Week 7 for the Packers.
articles.body:
Multiple other women contacted police to report abuse allegations against Josh Jacobs while the Green Bay Packers running back was being investigated for a different incident in May, according to Northeast Wisconsin's NBC26 .

Previously unreleased files obtained by NBC26 on Friday show that the Hobart/Lawrence Police Department was contacted by at least three other women accusing Jacobs of abuse.

One woman contact police in June 2026 while they were investigating Jacobs. She told them that she had a prior experience with Jacobs in January 2022 that sounded similar. The woman did not originally make a report with police, but came forward because she felt her incident could help with the current case.

The woman alleged that Jacobs slapped her in the face and took her cellphone as she tried to leave his home, according to the records. She told investigators that Jacobs grabbed her by the hair, pinned her down on a bed and later threw her onto the floor, while also spitting on her and grabbing her by the throat.

After meeting Jacobs through Instagram, the woman said the two spoke for six months before meeting in person. After the alleged incident, she said they remained friends and that she did not want to report him to police.

That same month another woman contacted police telling them that Jacobs grabbed her arms, pushed her against a wall and threw items of hers outside of the home in April 2021. The woman said she had swelling by her rib area and suffered bruising to her arms. She contacted police at the time and said she was told the incident was not being investigated as a domestic incident because the two were not in a relationship.

A third woman called Hobart/Lawrence Police in May 2022 to report that Jacobs grabbed her by the head, dragged her, scratched her chest, and took her phone after it fell on the floor. That woman said she had bruising on her arm and scratches on her chest and that she did not report what happened to police at the time because she felt she could be deported.

"The Brown County District Attorney's office had these uncorroborated, old, and previously unreported allegations for months," Jacobs' attorneys said in a statement . "They conducted their own exhaustive investigation, along with the police department, and the D.A. determined that only two misdemeanor charges were warranted. They then entered into a plea agreement with Josh Jacobs. Josh has repeatedly expressed his remorse and is honoring the terms of the agreement."

Jacobs was arrested in northern Wisconsin on May 26 and charged with multiple counts of domestic abuse. The charges stemmed from an incident three days prior, when Jacobs allegedly grabbed a woman trying to leave his garage and threw her to the ground. He was formally charged with two of those counts, battery and criminal damage to property, the week before he was placed on the commissioner's exempt list and missed the first six weeks of the NFL season. He pleaded no contest to both charges .

The NFL could still hand down a suspension to Jacobs, who returned to play in Week 7, for violating the league's personal conduct policy with these new accusations being considered.

"We will review these allegations as part of the investigation which has remained open," the NFL said in a statement on Saturday.

Predicting Every Team's Trade Deadline Strategy 🧠

"The Bolts are 0-6 but are telling teams Khalil Mack isn't available. It's hard to envision that remaining the case over the next 10 days," Jones reported.

Mack, 35, is playing this season on an expiring $18 million contract. He has about $4.4 million of that deal remaining in 2026, per Spotrac .

He has been on the field for 71 percent of the Chargers' defensive snaps this season while contributing three sacks, 19 tackles (five for loss) and six quarterback hits.

No team in league history has recovered from more than four straight season-opening losses to make a playoff bid, and the Chargers are heading into Week 8 as the lone winless team in the NFL.

articles.title: Commanders' Daron Payne suffers season-ending foot fracture
articles.summary: Washington Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne is officially out for the season after suffering a foot fracture in practice on Friday.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders simply cannot catch a break. Over the last two seasons, their roster has suffered significant, season-ending injuries across the board. In their Week 6 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers, the Commanders lost star wide receiver Terry McLaurin for the remainder of the season. Before that, Jayden Daniels re-injured his left elbow, and Athan Kaliakmanis debuted in the NFL when Marcus Mariota went down with a knee injury.

Those are just a few of the things this team has been handed in 2026, and now they're getting smacked in the mouth with another season-ending injury. On Friday, starting defensive tackle Daron Payne went down with a "significant" injury . Today, ESPN's Adam Schefter reports that Payne is, in fact, lost for the season with a fracture in his foot.

Payne, 29, is in his ninth NFL season after Washington made him the No. 13 overall pick in the 2018 NFL Draft. He has appeared in 136 career games for Washington, starting 130 and recording 446 tackles, including 67 for loss, 86 quarterback hits, 38 sacks, eight forced fumbles, six fumble recoveries and one interception. He made the Pro Bowl in 2022, which was his best NFL season. Payne finished that year with 64 tackles, 28 TFLs, 20 quarterback hits and 11.5 sacks. He signed a four-year extension that offseason and will be a free agent at the end of this season.

The Commanders' next challenge is on Sunday night when they host the Philadelphia Eagles , who are, incredibly, more banged up than Washington. Payne's loss makes getting Jer'Zhan Newton back to practice even more important, and they'll need him back in game shape as soon as possible.

Payne will become the eighth player to land on IR for the Commanders this season, and the most frustrating part is that it happened late in Friday's practice. His loss creates a huge hole on the defensive line, so be on the lookout for roster moves soon.

articles.title: Jake Bates Drops Bombshell About Longest Field Goal He’s Ever Made
articles.summary: Detroit Lions kicker Jake Bates reveals he once made a 75-yard field goal in practice and explains how his first successful game kick came from 64 yards.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions kicker Jake Bates has already proven he possesses one of the strongest legs in professional football, but his latest revelation might leave even the most diehard Lions fans shaking their heads.

During a recent appearance on the St. Brown Podcast , Bates revealed that he once connected on a field goal from approximately 75 yards while practicing with the Michigan Panthers of the UFL.

Now, before Lions fans start demanding that Dan Campbell send Bates onto the field for an NFL-record attempt, there is one important detail worth mentioning.

Still, the story behind that incredible kick is almost as remarkable as the distance itself. Especially when you consider that Bates went his entire high school and college careers without making a single field goal in a game.

Jake Bates Reveals Incredible 75-Yard Field Goal

During the interview, Bates was asked about the longest field goal he had ever made in practice. His answer certainly didn't disappoint.

"Probably like 75, with some wind at your back," Bates said during his appearance on the St. Brown Podcast . "You start feeling a little good, and you just start swinging for the fences."

Bates explained that the kick wasn't part of a structured practice drill. Instead, he and some teammates were simply having fun testing how far he could kick the football.

"I haven't really backed it up like that in a long time, but probably something like that," Bates continued. "I remember doing that in practice in the UFL. We were kind of screwing off on the field next to the practice field, just seeing how far we could swing at it."

Imagine casually messing around after practice and launching a football through the uprights from three-quarters of the length of the field.

Most kickers would be thrilled to make a 60-yarder. Bates apparently decided to see what happened when he kept backing up.

Bates' First Made Field Goal Came From 64 Yards

Perhaps the most incredible part of Bates' story is that his famous 64-yard game-winning field goal with the Michigan Panthers wasn't just the longest kick of his career at the time.

It was the first field goal he had ever successfully made in an actual game.

During the podcast, Bates explained that his football career began in unusual fashion.

"In high school, I joined the football team late my senior year after I had already committed to UCA, just because I had a couple friends on the team," Bates recalled. "Their kicker was pretty good, so I was like, 'I'll just kick off.'"

Bates wasn't exaggerating about his limited field-goal experience. He revealed that he attempted only two field goals in high school.

"I just kicked off, but they let me do long field goals, and I missed a 39 and a 47. I was 0-for-2 in high school."

That's right. The man who would eventually become an NFL kicker couldn't connect from 39 or 47 yards during his brief high school football career.

And things didn't change much when he reached college, where he continued handling kickoffs rather than serving as a traditional field-goal kicker.

Bates also mentioned making an extra point during a Houston Texans preseason appearance, but his spectacular 64-yarder with the Panthers remained his first successful field goal in a competitive game.

"That was the first one I had ever made," Bates explained. "There was a lot of wind in those games, though, but they were ugly kicks."

Not exactly the background you would expect from someone who eventually made it to the NFL.

Jake Bates' Longest Field Goal With Detroit Lions

Bates' remarkable UFL performance helped him earn an opportunity with the Lions, and he has since established himself as a reliable NFL kicker.

During the interview, he was asked about his longest successful field goal in the NFL.

That 59-yard field goal came during Detroit's 2025 season and remains his NFL career long, according to the Lions' official player statistics .

When asked whether his 64-yard UFL field goal remained the longest successful kick of his professional game career, Bates confirmed that it did.

"Yeah. I've had two chances at deep ones."

He also admitted that his unforgettable 64-yard kick had a little more distance available.

That's a pretty entertaining understatement from a guy who once blasted a ball through the uprights from approximately 75 yards in practice.

As we recently covered following Detroit's victory over Green Bay , the Lions continue preparing for another major NFC North matchup, and having a kicker with Bates' range gives Campbell an additional weapon in close games.

Of course, making a field goal from 75 yards with the wind at your back during a relaxed practice session is much different from attempting one with NFL defenders charging toward you.

But it does provide a pretty fascinating glimpse at just how much power Bates possesses.

From going 0-for-2 in high school to drilling a 64-yard game-winner on his first successful field-goal attempt, Bates has already enjoyed one of football's most unlikely journeys.

And if the Lions ever find themselves needing an absolutely ridiculous field goal with the wind blowing in the right direction, at least they know their kicker has tried something like it before.

articles.title: NFL removes officiating crew from ‘Sunday Night Football’ after poor showing
articles.summary: The NFL wasn’t able to flex Sunday night’s game between the Washington Commanders and Philadelphia Eagles out fo primetime, but it was able to move the unins...
articles.body:
The NFL wasn't able to flex Sunday night's game between the Washington Commanders and Philadelphia Eagles out fo primetime, but it was able to move the uninspiring officiating crew that was set to work the game.

Last week, NFL on Fox lead analyst Tom Brady criticized multiple flags from a crew led by referee Alex Moore during the game between the Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions, featured for most of the nation to see in the 4:25 p.m. ET late afternoon window.

On one particularly questionable unnecessary roughness call, Brady described the hit by saying, "That's allowed 99 out of 100."

"It's a bang-bang play," Brady added of the call. "I know in super slow-mo every little minute frame looks like a lot, but when you're on the field you've got to pursue that ball. If he catches that, he needs force to knock him on the ground. He needs force to knock that ball off him as a pass defense. He can't go in there and put his hand on him."

Now, according to a report from Football Zebras, Moore's crew has been moved out of the Sunday Night Football on NBC and will instead work the game between the New England Patriots and Miami Dolphins, which will be regionally televised. The crew led by white hat Shawn Hochuli will officiate the SNF game instead.

"Alex Moore's crew has been switched out of SNF and will officiate Patriots-Dolphins instead. Shawn Hochuli's crew has been moved to cover the primetime game in Washington. Officiating sources say the switch is more about optics rather than a disciplinary action," Football Zebras reported.

NFL officiating has been under unprecedented scrutiny this season. Not only has the wisdom of certain calls been questioned, but the sheer amount of penalty flags has impacted t the entertainment value of the games and has had an outsized impact on important plays and game results.

Officials are always going to make a few calls fans don't agree with, but it seems like the NFL has a good grasp on when those fans might have a legit case and is going to be proactive about dealing with struggling crews.

articles.title: Rams’ Aaron Donald Unbothered by Lack of Counting Stats
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams defensive end Aaron Donald is yet to record a sack this season, but the veteran isn't concerned by his lack of statistics. The post Rams’ Aa...
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams defensive end Aaron Donald is yet to record a sack this season, but the veteran isn't concerned by his lack of statistics.

"No. I didn't come back for individual stats," Donald said on whether or not his lack of sacks bothered him. "I would love to have some stats, but I'm here to just play the game. When the plays present themselves, take advantage of it, try to get my plays, but my main focus is trying to find ways to help this team win.

"That's the goal. I didn't come back to try to earn individual accolades or anything. I did that, accomplished that. It doesn't excite me. The only thing that excites me is winning so I'm just playing a football game, trying to do what I can to help this team. As long as we win, I can build off everything else and get myself better off that."

Donald spent 10 seasons with the Rams from 2014-23, retiring at the end of the 2023 season. With the Rams, Donald won everything there was to win. He brought the team a Super Bowl and earned three Defensive Player of the Year awards as well as 10 Pro Bowl selections.

He made an unprecedented return from retirement this offseason, joining Myles Garrett—who has only played one game so far—after the Rams traded for him, but the team's results are yet to show. The Rams currently sit at 3-4, third in the NFC West, though their defense has been stellar. While he doesn't have a sack, Garrett has two tackles for loss and 10 total tackles on the season, as well as a fumble recovery.

Did Aaron Donald Ever Finish a Season Without a Sack?

While Donald is yet to record a sack, history shows he's going to break out of that drought sooner rather than later.

Over the first 10 seasons of his career, Donald never logged fewer than five sacks in a season, and had as many as 20.5 during those years. He clearly has the knowledge and ability to break out, and it's only a matter of time until he does so.

Donald's next opportunity to make a difference and help the Rams win comes Sunday, when they face off against the Los Angeles Chargers at 1:25 p.m. PT.
